verses.textEnNlt: Then she said, "Please swear to me by the Lord your God that you won’t let anyone take vengeance against my son. I want no more bloodshed." "As surely as the Lord lives," he replied, "not a hair on your son’s head will be disturbed!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then she said, "May the king please remember the Lord your God, so that the avenger of blood will not continue to destroy, otherwise they will destroy my son." And he said, "As the Lord lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
verses.textEn: She said, "Then let the king invoke the Lord his God to prevent the avenger of blood from adding to the destruction, so that my son will not be destroyed." "As surely as the Lord lives," he said, "not one hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground."

verses.textZh: 那妇人又说："请允许婢女对我主我王再说一句话。"王说："你说吧。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 那妇人又说："请允许婢女对我主我王再说一句话。"王说："你说吧。"
verses.textZhCuv: 妇人说：「求我主我王容婢女再说一句话。」王说：「你说吧！」
verses.textEnNiv: Then the woman said, "Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." "Speak," he replied.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the woman said, "Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." He said, "Speak."
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore the woman said, "Please, let your maidservant speak another word to my lord the king." And he said, "Say on."
verses.textEnNlt: "Please allow me to ask one more thing of my lord the king," she said. "Go ahead and speak," he responded.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the woman said, "Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
verses.textEn: Then the woman said, "Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." "Speak," he replied.

verses.textZh: 妇人说："你为甚么想出这样的事来陷害神的子民呢？王说了这话，如果不让自己逃亡的人回来，就是个有罪的人了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 妇人说："你为甚么想出这样的事来陷害神的子民呢？王说了这话，如果不让自己逃亡的人回来，就是个有罪的人了。
verses.textZhCuv: 妇人说：「王为何也起意要害神的民呢？王不使那逃亡的人回来，王的这话就是自证己错了！
verses.textEnNiv: The woman said, "Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?
verses.textEnEsv: And the woman said, "Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in giving this decision the king convicts himself, inasmuch as the king does not bring his banished one home again.
verses.textEnNkjv: So the woman said: "Why then have you schemed such a thing against the people of God? For the king speaks this thing as one who is guilty, inthat the king does not bring his banished one home again.
verses.textEnNlt: She replied, "Why don’t you do as much for the people of God as you have promised to do for me? You have convicted yourself in making this decision, because you have refused to bring home your own banished son.
verses.textEnNasb: The woman said, "Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is like one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring back his banished one.
verses.textEn: The woman said, "Why then have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, for the king has not brought back his banished son?

verses.textZh: 我们都是必死的，像水泼在地上不能收回来一样；但神并不取去人的命，反而设法使逃亡的人不致永远离开他逃亡。
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们都是必死的，像水泼在地上不能收回来一样；但神并不取去人的命，反而设法使逃亡的人不致永远离开他逃亡。
verses.textZhCuv: 我们都是必死的，如同水泼在地上，不能收回。神并不夺取人的性命，乃设法使逃亡的人不致成为赶出、回不来的。
verses.textEnNiv: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But that is not what God desires; rather, he devises ways so that a banished person does not remain banished from him.
verses.textEnEsv: We must all die; we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But God will not take away life, and he devises means so that the banished one will not remain an outcast.
verses.textEnNkjv: For we will surely die and become like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. Yet God does not take away a life; but He devises means, so that His banished ones are not expelled from Him.
verses.textEnNlt: All of us must die eventually. Our lives are like water spilled out on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But God does not just sweep life away; instead, he devises ways to bring us back when we have been separated from him.
verses.textEnNasb: For we will surely die and are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up. Yet God does not take away life, but makes plans so that the banished one will not be cast out from Him.
verses.textEn: Like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be recovered, so we must die. But that is not what God desires; rather, he devises ways so that a banished person does not remain banished from him.

verses.textZh: 现在我来对我主我王说这话，是因为众民使我害怕，所以婢女想：‘现在我要对王说，也许王会成全婢女所求的。’
verses.textZhCnvs: 现在我来对我主我王说这话，是因为众民使我害怕，所以婢女想：‘现在我要对王说，也许王会成全婢女所求的。’
verses.textZhCuv: 我来将这话告诉我主我王，是因百姓使我惧怕。婢女想，不如将这话告诉王，或者王成就婢女所求的。
verses.textEnNiv: "And now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king; perhaps he will grant his servant’s request.
verses.textEnEsv: Now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid, and your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now therefore, I have come to speak of this thing to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. And your maidservant said, ‘I will now speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his maidservant.
verses.textEnNlt: "I have come to plead with my lord the king because people have threatened me. I said to myself, ‘Perhaps the king will listen to me
verses.textEnNasb: Now then, the reason I have come to speak this word to my lord the king is that the people have made me afraid; so your servant said, ‘Let me now speak to the king, perhaps the king will perform the request of his slave.
verses.textEn: "And now I have come to say this to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king; perhaps he will grant his servant’s request.

verses.textZh: 人要把我和我的儿子从神的产业上一同消灭，也许王会垂听，会把婢女从那人的手下救出来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 人要把我和我的儿子从神的产业上一同消灭，也许王会垂听，会把婢女从那人的手下救出来。
verses.textZhCuv: 人要将我和我儿子从神的地业上一同除灭，王必应允救我脱离他的手。
verses.textEnNiv: Perhaps the king will agree to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who is trying to cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
verses.textEnEsv: For the king will hear and deliver his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together from the heritage of God.’
verses.textEnNkjv: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man whowould destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.’
verses.textEnNlt: and rescue us from those who would cut us off from the inheritance God has given us.
verses.textEnNasb: For the king will listen, to save his slave from the hand of the man who would eliminate both me and my son from the inheritance of God.’
verses.textEn: Perhaps the king will agree to deliver his servant from the hand of the man who is trying to cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’

verses.textZh: 婢女又想：‘我主我王的话必能使我得安慰，因为我主我王像神的使者一样，能分辨是非。愿耶和华你的神与你同在。’"
verses.textZhCnvs: 婢女又想：‘我主我王的话必能使我得安慰，因为我主我王像神的使者一样，能分辨是非。愿耶和华你的神与你同在。’"
verses.textZhCuv: 婢女又想，我主我王的话必安慰我；因为我主我王能辨别是非，如同神的使者一样。惟愿耶和华－你的神与你同在！」
verses.textEnNiv: "And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king secure my inheritance, for my lord the king is like an angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the Lord your God be with you.’ "
verses.textEnEsv: And your servant thought, ‘The word of my lord the king will set me at rest,’ for my lord the king is like the angel of God to discern good and evil. The Lord your God be with you!"
verses.textEnNkjv: Your maidservant said, ‘The word of my lord the king will now be comforting; for as the angel of God, so is my lord the king in discerning good and evil. And may the Lord your God be with you.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: Yes, my lord the king will give us peace of mind again.’ I know that you are like an angel of God in discerning good from evil. May the Lord your God be with you."
verses.textEnNasb: Then your servant said, ‘Please let the word of my lord the king be comforting, for as the angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and evil. And may the Lord your God be with you.’ "
verses.textEn: "And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king secure my inheritance, for my lord the king is like an angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the Lord your God be with you.’ "

verses.textZh: 王对那妇人说："我要问你一句话，请你不要瞒我。"妇人回答："我主我王，请说！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对那妇人说："我要问你一句话，请你不要瞒我。"妇人回答："我主我王，请说！"
verses.textZhCuv: 王对妇人说：「我要问你一句话，你一点不要瞒我。」妇人说：「愿我主我王说。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then the king said to the woman, "Don’t keep from me the answer to what I am going to ask you." "Let my lord the king speak," the woman said.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king answered the woman, "Do not hide from me anything I ask you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not hide from me anything that I ask you." And the woman said, "Please, let my lord the king speak."
verses.textEnNlt: "I must know one thing," the king replied, "and tell me the truth." "Yes, my lord the king," she responded.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not hide anything from me that I am about to ask you." And the woman said, "Let my lord the king please speak."
verses.textEn: Then the king said to the woman, "Don’t keep from me the answer to what I am going to ask you." "Let my lord the king speak," the woman said.

verses.textZh: 王问："这一切都是约押一手安排的吗？"妇人回答："我指着我主我王起誓，王所说的丝毫不差。这正是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这一切话也都是他教婢女说的。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王问："这一切都是约押一手安排的吗？"妇人回答："我指着我主我王起誓，王所说的丝毫不差。这正是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这一切话也都是他教婢女说的。
verses.textZhCuv: 王说：「你这些话莫非是约押的主意吗？」妇人说：「我敢在我主我王面前起誓：王的话正对，不偏左右，是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这些话是他教导我的。
verses.textEnNiv: The king asked, "Isn’t the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king says. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me to do this and who put all these words into the mouth of your servant.
verses.textEnEsv: The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered and said, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, one cannot turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has said. It was your servant Joab who commanded me; it was he who put all these words in the mouth of your servant.
verses.textEnNkjv: So the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman answered and said, "As you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken. For your servant Joab commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your maidservant.
verses.textEnNlt: "Did Joab put you up to this?" And the woman replied, "My lord the king, how can I deny it? Nobody can hide anything from you. Yes, Joab sent me and told me what to say.
verses.textEnNasb: So the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman replied, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken. Indeed, it was your servant Joab who commanded me, and it was he who put all these words in the mouth of your servant.
verses.textEn: The king asked, "Isn’t the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king says. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me to do this and who put all these words into the mouth of your servant.

verses.textZh: 王的仆人约押这样作，为要挽回这件事。我主有智慧，像神使者的智慧一样，能知道世上的一切事。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王的仆人约押这样作，为要挽回这件事。我主有智慧，像神使者的智慧一样，能知道世上的一切事。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王的仆人约押如此行，为要挽回这事。我主的智慧却如神使者的智慧，能知世上一切事。」
verses.textEnNiv: Your servant Joab did this to change the present situation. My lord has wisdom like that of an angel of God—he knows everything that happens in the land."
verses.textEnEsv: In order to change the course of things your servant Joab did this. But my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God to know all things that are on the earth."
verses.textEnNkjv: To bring about this change of affairs your servant Joab has done this thing; but my lord is wise, according to the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that is in the earth."
verses.textEnNlt: He did it to place the matter before you in a different light. But you are as wise as an angel of God, and you understand everything that happens among us!"
verses.textEnNasb: In order to change the appearance of things your servant Joab has done this thing. But my lord is wise, like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know all that is on the earth."
verses.textEn: Your servant Joab did this to change the present situation. My lord has wisdom like that of an angel of God—he knows everything that happens in the land."

verses.textZh: 王对约押说："看哪！这事我已经同意了。你去把那年轻人押沙龙带回来吧！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对约押说："看哪！这事我已经同意了。你去把那年轻人押沙龙带回来吧！"
verses.textZhCuv: 王对约押说：「我应允你这事。你可以去，把那少年人押沙龙带回来。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king said to Joab, "Very well, I will do it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king said to Joab, "Behold now, I grant this; go, bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said to Joab, "All right, I have granted this thing. Go therefore, bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.textEnNlt: So the king sent for Joab and told him, "All right, go and bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king said to Joab, "Behold now, I will certainly do this thing; go then, bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.textEn: The king said to Joab, "Very well, I will do it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."

verses.textZh: 约押就面伏于地，叩拜王，为王祝福；又说："今天你仆人知道在我主我王眼前蒙了恩宠，因为王成全了你仆人所求的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 约押就面伏于地，叩拜王，为王祝福；又说："今天你仆人知道在我主我王眼前蒙了恩宠，因为王成全了你仆人所求的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 约押就面伏于地叩拜，祝谢于王，又说：「王既应允仆人所求的，仆人今日知道在我主我王眼前蒙恩了。」
verses.textEnNiv: Joab fell with his face to the ground to pay him honor, and he blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant’s request."
verses.textEnEsv: And Joab fell on his face to the ground and paid homage and blessed the king. And Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has granted the request of his servant."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Joab fell to the ground on his face and bowed himself, and thanked the king. And Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord, O king, in that the king has fulfilled the request of his servant."
verses.textEnNlt: Joab bowed with his face to the ground in deep respect and said, "At last I know that I have gained your approval, my lord the king, for you have granted me this request!"
verses.textEnNasb: And Joab fell on his face to the ground, prostrated himself, and blessed the king; then Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has performed the request of his servant."
verses.textEn: Joab fell with his face to the ground to pay him honor, and he blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant’s request."

verses.textZh: 于是约押起来，往基述去，把押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是约押起来，往基述去，把押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是约押起身往基述去，将押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。
verses.textEnNiv: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnEsv: So Joab arose and went to Geshur and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNlt: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: Then Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

verses.textZh: 王说："让他回自己的家里去，不要见王的面。"押沙龙就转回自己的家里去，没有见王的面。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王说："让他回自己的家里去，不要见王的面。"押沙龙就转回自己的家里去，没有见王的面。
verses.textZhCuv: 王说：「使他回自己家里去，不要见我的面。」押沙龙就回自己家里去，没有见王的面。
verses.textEnNiv: But the king said, "He must go to his own house; he must not see my face." So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the face of the king.
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said, "Let him dwell apart in his own house; he is not to come into my presence." So Absalom lived apart in his own house and did not come into the king’s presence.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said, "Let him return to his own house, but do not let him see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house, but did not see the king’s face.
verses.textEnNlt: But the king gave this order: "Absalom may go to his own house, but he must never come into my presence." So Absalom did not see the king.
verses.textEnNasb: However, the king said, "He shall return to his own house, but he shall not see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house and did not see the king’s face.
verses.textEn: But the king said, "He must go to his own house; he must not see my face." So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the face of the king.

verses.textZh: 在全以色列中，没有一个人像押沙龙那样英俊，得人称赞，从脚底到头顶，都没有一点缺陷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 在全以色列中，没有一个人像押沙龙那样英俊，得人称赞，从脚底到头顶，都没有一点缺陷。
verses.textZhCuv: 以色列全地之中，无人像押沙龙那样俊美，得人的称赞，从脚底到头顶毫无瑕疵。
verses.textEnNiv: In all Israel there was not a man so highly praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the top of his head to the sole of his foot there was no blemish in him.
verses.textEnEsv: Now in all Israel there was no one so much to be praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now in all Israel there was no one who was praised as much as Absalom for his good looks. From the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.textEnNlt: Now Absalom was praised as the most handsome man in all Israel. He was flawless from head to foot.
verses.textEnNasb: Now in all Israel there was no one as handsome as Absalom, so highly praised; from the sole of his foot to the top of his head there was no impairment in him.
verses.textEn: In all Israel there was not a man so highly praised for his handsome appearance as Absalom. From the top of his head to the sole of his foot there was no blemish in him.

verses.textZh: 他每年年底剪发一次，因为他头上的头发太厚，所以把它剪下来；他把头发剪下来以后，总是把头发称一称；按照王的法码重约两公斤。
verses.textZhCnvs: 他每年年底剪发一次，因为他头上的头发太厚，所以把它剪下来；他把头发剪下来以后，总是把头发称一称；按照王的法码重约两公斤。
verses.textZhCuv: 他的头发甚重，每到年底剪发一次；所剪下来的，按王的平称一称，重二百舍客勒。
verses.textEnNiv: Whenever he cut the hair of his head—he used to cut his hair once a year because it became too heavy for him—he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.
verses.textEnEsv: And when he cut the hair of his head (for at the end of every year he used to cut it; when it was heavy on him, he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head, two hundred shekels by the king’s weight.
verses.textEnNkjv: And when he cut the hair of his head—at the end of every year he cut it because it was heavy on him—when he cut it, he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels according to the king’s standard.
verses.textEnNlt: He cut his hair only once a year, and then only because it was so heavy. When he weighed it out, it came to five pounds!
verses.textEnNasb: And when he cut the hair of his head (and it was at the end of every year that he cut it, because it was heavy on him, so he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the king’s weight.
verses.textEn: Whenever he cut the hair of his head—he used to cut his hair once a year because it became too heavy for him—he would weigh it, and its weight was two hundred shekels by the royal standard.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫他玛，是个容貌美丽的女子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫他玛，是个容貌美丽的女子。
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫她玛，是个容貌俊美的女子。
verses.textEnNiv: Three sons and a daughter were born to Absalom. His daughter’s name was Tamar, and she became a beautiful woman.
verses.textEnEsv: There were born to Absalom three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a beautiful woman.
verses.textEnNkjv: To Absalom were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar. She was a woman of beautiful appearance.
verses.textEnNlt: He had three sons and one daughter. His daughter’s name was Tamar, and she was very beautiful.
verses.textEnNasb: And to Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar; she was a woman of beautiful appearance.
verses.textEn: Three sons and a daughter were born to Absalom. His daughter’s name was Tamar, and she became a beautiful woman.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷住了两年，都没有见王的面。
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷住了两年，都没有见王的面。
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙住在耶路撒冷足有二年，没有见王的面。
verses.textEnNiv: Absalom lived two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face.
verses.textEnEsv: So Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, without coming into the king’s presence.
verses.textEnNkjv: And Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, but did not see the king’s face.
verses.textEnNlt: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years, but he never got to see the king.
verses.textEnNasb: Now Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, yet he did not see the king’s face.
verses.textEn: Absalom lived two years in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙派人去叫约押来，要托他去见王，约押却不肯来见他。他第二次再派人去叫他，他还是不肯来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙派人去叫约押来，要托他去见王，约押却不肯来见他。他第二次再派人去叫他，他还是不肯来。
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙打发人去叫约押来，要托他去见王，约押却不肯来。第二次打发人去叫他，他仍不肯来。
verses.textEnNiv: Then Absalom sent for Joab in order to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So he sent a second time, but he refused to come.
verses.textEnEsv: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but Joab would not come to him. And he sent a second time, but Joab would not come.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. And when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
verses.textEnNlt: Then Absalom sent for Joab to ask him to intercede for him, but Joab refused to come. Absalom sent for him a second time, but again Joab refused to come.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. So he sent word again a second time, but he would not come.
verses.textEn: Then Absalom sent for Joab in order to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him. So he sent a second time, but he refused to come.

verses.textZh: 于是押沙龙对仆人说："你们看，约押的一块田和我相邻，田里有大麦。你们去放火烧田！"押沙龙的仆人就放火把那块田烧了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是押沙龙对仆人说："你们看，约押的一块田和我相邻，田里有大麦。你们去放火烧田！"押沙龙的仆人就放火把那块田烧了。
verses.textZhCuv: 所以押沙龙对仆人说：「你们看，约押有一块田，与我的田相近，其中有大麦，你们去放火烧了。」押沙龙的仆人就去放火烧了那田。
verses.textEnNiv: Then he said to his servants, "Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
verses.textEnEsv: Then he said to his servants, "See, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
verses.textEnNkjv: So he said to his servants, "See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
verses.textEnNlt: So Absalom said to his servants, "Go and set fire to Joab’s barley field, the field next to mine." So they set his field on fire, as Absalom had commanded.
verses.textEnNasb: Therefore he said to his servants, "See, Joab’s plot is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." So Absalom’s servants set the plot on fire.
verses.textEn: Then he said to his servants, "Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

verses.textZh: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙的家，问他："你的仆人为甚么放火烧了我那块田呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙的家，问他："你的仆人为甚么放火烧了我那块田呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙家里，问他说：「你的仆人为何放火烧了我的田呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Joab did go to Absalom’s house, and he said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.textEnEsv: Then Joab arose and went to Absalom at his house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Joab arose and came to Absalom’s house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.textEnNlt: Then Joab came to Absalom at his house and demanded, "Why did your servants set my field on fire?"
verses.textEnNasb: Then Joab got up, came to Absalom at his house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my plot on fire?"
verses.textEn: Then Joab did go to Absalom’s house, and he said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

verses.textZh: 押沙龙回答约押："看哪，我派人去见你，说：‘请你到这里来，我要托你去见王，替我说："我为甚么从基述回来呢？我若是还留在那边，会觉得更好。"’现在，我要见王的面，如果我有罪，任由他把我杀死好了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙回答约押："看哪，我派人去见你，说：‘请你到这里来，我要托你去见王，替我说："我为甚么从基述回来呢？我若是还留在那边，会觉得更好。"’现在，我要见王的面，如果我有罪，任由他把我杀死好了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙回答约押说：「我打发人去请你来，好托你去见王，替我说：『我为何从基述回来呢？不如仍在那里。』现在要许我见王的面；我若有罪，任凭王杀我就是了。」
verses.textEnNiv: Absalom said to Joab, "Look, I sent word to you and said, ‘Come here so I can send you to the king to ask, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there!" ’ Now then, I want to see the king’s face, and if I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death."
verses.textEnEsv: Absalom answered Joab, "Behold, I sent word to you, ‘Come here, that I may send you to the king, to ask, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still." Now therefore let me go into the presence of the king, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death.’"
verses.textEnNkjv: And Absalom answered Joab, "Look, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I may send you to the king, to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? Itwouldbe better for me tobe there still." ’ Now therefore, let me see the king’s face; but if there is iniquity in me, let him execute me."
verses.textEnNlt: And Absalom replied, "Because I wanted you to ask the king why he brought me back from Geshur if he didn’t intend to see me. I might as well have stayed there. Let me see the king; if he finds me guilty of anything, then let him kill me."
verses.textEnNasb: Absalom answered Joab, "Behold, I sent for you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I may send you to the king, to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me still to be there." ’ Now then, let me see the king’s face, and if there is guilt in me, he can have me executed."
verses.textEn: Absalom said to Joab, "Look, I sent word to you and said, ‘Come here so I can send you to the king to ask, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there!" ’ Now then, I want to see the king’s face, and if I am guilty of anything, let him put me to death."

verses.textZh: 于是约押进去见王，把这事告诉了他，王就召见押沙龙。押沙龙进去见王，在王面前脸伏在地拜他，王就与押沙龙亲吻。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是约押进去见王，把这事告诉了他，王就召见押沙龙。押沙龙进去见王，在王面前脸伏在地拜他，王就与押沙龙亲吻。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是约押去见王，将这话奏告王，王便叫押沙龙来。押沙龙来见王，在王面前俯伏于地，王就与押沙龙亲嘴。
verses.textEnNiv: So Joab went to the king and told him this. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
verses.textEnEsv: Then Joab went to the king and told him, and he summoned Absalom. So he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.textEnNkjv: So Joab went to the king and told him. And when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king. Then the king kissed Absalom.
verses.textEnNlt: So Joab told the king what Absalom had said. Then at last David summoned Absalom, who came and bowed low before the king, and the king kissed him.
verses.textEnNasb: So when Joab came to the king and told him, he summoned Absalom. Then Absalom came to the king and prostrated himself with his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.textEn: So Joab went to the king and told him this. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed down with his face to the ground before the king. And the king kissed Absalom.

verses.textZh: 这事以后，押沙龙为自己预备了一辆战车和一些马匹，又预备了五十人在他前面奔走开路。
verses.textZhCnvs: 这事以后，押沙龙为自己预备了一辆战车和一些马匹，又预备了五十人在他前面奔走开路。
verses.textZhCuv: 此后，押沙龙为自己预备车马，又派五十人在他前头奔走。
verses.textEnNiv: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.
verses.textEnEsv: After this Absalom got himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.textEnNkjv: After this it happened that Absalom provided himself with chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.textEnNlt: After this, Absalom bought a chariot and horses, and he hired fifty bodyguards to run ahead of him.
verses.textEnNasb: Now it came about after this that Absalom provided for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
verses.textEn: In the course of time, Absalom provided himself with a chariot and horses and with fifty men to run ahead of him.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙常常清早起来，站在通往城门口的路旁。有争讼的案件要进去请王判决的人，押沙龙就把他叫到跟前来，问他："你是从哪一座城来的？"他回答："仆人是从以色列某一支派来的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙常常清早起来，站在通往城门口的路旁。有争讼的案件要进去请王判决的人，押沙龙就把他叫到跟前来，问他："你是从哪一座城来的？"他回答："仆人是从以色列某一支派来的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙常常早晨起来，站在城门的道旁，凡有争讼要去求王判断的，押沙龙就叫他过来，问他说：「你是哪一城的人？」回答说：「仆人是以色列某支派的人。」
verses.textEnNiv: He would get up early and stand by the side of the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a complaint to be placed before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, "What town are you from?" He would answer, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.textEnEsv: And Absalom used to rise early and stand beside the way of the gate. And when any man had a dispute to come before the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "From what city are you?" And when he said, "Your servant is of such and such a tribe in Israel,"
verses.textEnNkjv: Now Absalom would rise early and stand beside the way to the gate. So it was, whenever anyone who had a lawsuit came to the king for a decision, that Absalom would call to him and say, "What city are you from?" And he would say, "Your servant is from such and such a tribe of Israel."
verses.textEnNlt: He got up early every morning and went out to the gate of the city. When people brought a case to the king for judgment, Absalom would ask where in Israel they were from, and they would tell him their tribe.
verses.textEnNasb: And Absalom used to rise early and stand beside the road to the gate; and when any man who had a lawsuit was to come before the king for judgment, Absalom would call out to him and say, "From what city are you?" And he would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.textEn: He would get up early and stand by the side of the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a complaint to be placed before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out to him, "What town are you from?" He would answer, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."

verses.textZh: 押沙龙就对他说："你看！你的案件有情有理，但是王并没有委人听你的案子。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙就对他说："你看！你的案件有情有理，但是王并没有委人听你的案子。"
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙对他说：「你的事有情有理，无奈王没有委人听你伸诉。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Absalom would say to him, "Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you."
verses.textEnEsv: Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no man designated by the king to hear you."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Absalom would say to him, "Look, your case is good and right; but thereis no deputy of the king to hear you."
verses.textEnNlt: Then Absalom would say, "You’ve really got a strong case here! It’s too bad the king doesn’t have anyone to hear it.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but you have no one to listen to you on the part of the king."
verses.textEn: Then Absalom would say to him, "Look, your claims are valid and proper, but there is no representative of the king to hear you."

verses.textZh: 押沙龙又说："但愿有人立我作这地的审判官，这样，有案件或诉讼的人，都可以到我这里来，我就给他公平的审判。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙又说："但愿有人立我作这地的审判官，这样，有案件或诉讼的人，都可以到我这里来，我就给他公平的审判。"
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙又说：「恨不得我作国中的士师！凡有争讼求审判的到我这里来，我必秉公判断。」
verses.textEnNiv: And Absalom would add, "If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me and I would see that they receive justice."
verses.textEnEsv: Then Absalom would say, "Oh that I were judge in the land! Then every man with a dispute or cause might come to me, and I would give him justice."
verses.textEnNkjv: Moreover Absalom would say, "Oh, that I were made judge in the land, and everyone who has any suit or cause would come to me; then I would give him justice."
verses.textEnNlt: I wish I were the judge. Then everyone could bring their cases to me for judgment, and I would give them justice!"
verses.textEnNasb: Moreover, Absalom would say, "Oh that someone would appoint me judge in the land, then every man who has a lawsuit or claim could come to me, and I would give him justice!"
verses.textEn: And Absalom would add, "If only I were appointed judge in the land! Then everyone who has a complaint or case could come to me and I would see that they receive justice."

verses.textZh: 如果有人走近押沙龙要拜他，他就伸手拉住他，并且与他亲吻。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果有人走近押沙龙要拜他，他就伸手拉住他，并且与他亲吻。
verses.textZhCuv: 若有人近前来要拜押沙龙，押沙龙就伸手拉住他，与他亲嘴。
verses.textEnNiv: Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.
verses.textEnEsv: And whenever a man came near to pay homage to him, he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.
verses.textEnNkjv: And so it was, whenever anyone came near to bow down to him, that he would put out his hand and take him and kiss him.
verses.textEnNlt: When people tried to bow before him, Absalom wouldn’t let them. Instead, he took them by the hand and kissed them.
verses.textEnNasb: And whenever a man approached to prostrate himself before him, he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.
verses.textEn: Also, whenever anyone approached him to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him and kiss him.

verses.textZh: 所有来到王面前请求审决的以色列人，押沙龙都是这样对待他们。因此，押沙龙暗中迷惑了以色列人的心。
verses.textZhCnvs: 所有来到王面前请求审决的以色列人，押沙龙都是这样对待他们。因此，押沙龙暗中迷惑了以色列人的心。
verses.textZhCuv: 以色列人中，凡去见王求判断的，押沙龙都是如此待他们。这样，押沙龙暗中得了以色列人的心。
verses.textEnNiv: Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king asking for justice, and so he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
verses.textEnEsv: Thus Absalom did to all of Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
verses.textEnNkjv: In this manner Absalom acted toward all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
verses.textEnNlt: Absalom did this with everyone who came to the king for judgment, and so he stole the hearts of all the people of Israel.
verses.textEnNasb: Absalom dealt this way with all Israel who came to the king for judgment; so Absalom stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
verses.textEn: Absalom behaved in this way toward all the Israelites who came to the king asking for justice, and so he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.

verses.textZh: 过了四年 ，押沙龙对王说："求你准我到希伯仑去，好向耶和华还我所许的愿。
verses.textZhCnvs: 过了四年 ，押沙龙对王说："求你准我到希伯仑去，好向耶和华还我所许的愿。
verses.textZhCuv: 满了四十年 ，押沙龙对王说：「求你准我往希伯仑去，还我向耶和华所许的愿。
verses.textEnNiv: At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, "Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the Lord .
verses.textEnEsv: And at the end of four years Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to the Lord , in Hebron.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now it came to pass after forty years that Absalom said to the king, "Please, let me go to Hebron and pay the vow which I made to the Lord.
verses.textEnNlt: After four years, Absalom said to the king, "Let me go to Hebron to offer a sacrifice to the Lord and fulfill a vow I made to him.
verses.textEnNasb: Now it came about at the end of four years that Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow which I have made to the Lord, in Hebron.
verses.textEn: At the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, "Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to the Lord .

verses.textZh: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述的时候，曾经许了一个愿说：‘如果耶和华使我再回到耶路撒冷来，我就要在希伯仑事奉他。’"
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述的时候，曾经许了一个愿说：‘如果耶和华使我再回到耶路撒冷来，我就要在希伯仑事奉他。’"
verses.textZhCuv: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述，曾许愿说：『耶和华若使我再回耶路撒冷，我必事奉他。』」
verses.textEnNiv: While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: ‘If the Lord takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord in Hebron. ’ "
verses.textEnEsv: For your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘If the Lord will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will offer worship to the Lord .’"
verses.textEnNkjv: For your servant took a vow while I dwelt at Geshur in Syria, saying, ‘If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: For while your servant was at Geshur in Aram, I promised to sacrifice to the Lord in Hebron if he would bring me back to Jerusalem."
verses.textEnNasb: For your servant made a vow while I was living in Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘If the Lord will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.’ "
verses.textEn: While your servant was living at Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: ‘If the Lord takes me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord in Hebron. ’ "

verses.textZh: 王对他说："你平平安安地去吧！"于是他动身，往希伯仑去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对他说："你平平安安地去吧！"于是他动身，往希伯仑去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 王说：「你平平安安地去吧！」押沙龙就起身，往希伯仑去了。
verses.textEnNiv: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he went to Hebron.
verses.textEnEsv: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said to him, "Go in peace." So he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.textEnNlt: "All right," the king told him. "Go and fulfill your vow." So Absalom went to Hebron.
verses.textEnNasb: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he got up and went to Hebron.
verses.textEn: The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he went to Hebron.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙派遣探子到以色列的各支派中，说："你们一听见号角的声音，就说：‘押沙龙在希伯仑作王了！’"
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙派遣探子到以色列的各支派中，说："你们一听见号角的声音，就说：‘押沙龙在希伯仑作王了！’"
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙打发探子走遍以色列各支派，说：「你们一听见角声就说：『押沙龙在希伯仑作王了！』」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron.’ "
verses.textEnEsv: But Absalom sent secret messengers throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, ‘Absalom is king at Hebron!’"
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’ "
verses.textEnNlt: But while he was there, he sent secret messengers to all the tribes of Israel to stir up a rebellion against the king. "As soon as you hear the ram’s horn," his message read, "you are to say, ‘Absalom has been crowned king in Hebron.’"
verses.textEnNasb: But Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’ "
verses.textEn: Then Absalom sent secret messengers throughout the tribes of Israel to say, "As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpets, then say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron.’ "

verses.textZh: 有二百人从耶路撒冷应邀与押沙龙同去。他们都是诚诚实实地去，对内情一点也不知道。
verses.textZhCnvs: 有二百人从耶路撒冷应邀与押沙龙同去。他们都是诚诚实实地去，对内情一点也不知道。
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷请了二百人与他同去，都是诚诚实实去的，并不知道其中的真情。
verses.textEnNiv: Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter.
verses.textEnEsv: With Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who were invited guests, and they went in their innocence and knew nothing.
verses.textEnNkjv: And with Absalom went two hundred men invited from Jerusalem, and they went along innocently and did not know anything.
verses.textEnNlt: He took 200 men from Jerusalem with him as guests, but they knew nothing of his intentions.
verses.textEnNasb: Then two hundred men went with Absalom from Jerusalem, who were invited and went innocently, for they did not know anything.
verses.textEn: Two hundred men from Jerusalem had accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went quite innocently, knowing nothing about the matter.

verses.textZh: 押沙龙献祭的时候，差派人去把大卫的参谋基罗人亚希多弗从他的本城基罗请来。于是叛乱的势力越来越大，跟随押沙龙的人民也越来越多。
verses.textZhCnvs: 押沙龙献祭的时候，差派人去把大卫的参谋基罗人亚希多弗从他的本城基罗请来。于是叛乱的势力越来越大，跟随押沙龙的人民也越来越多。
verses.textZhCuv: 押沙龙献祭的时候，打发人去将大卫的谋士、基罗人亚希多弗从他本城请了来。于是叛逆的势派甚大；因为随从押沙龙的人民，日渐增多。
verses.textEnNiv: While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from Giloh, his hometown. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept on increasing.
verses.textEnEsv: And while Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city Giloh. And the conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city—from Giloh—while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy grew strong, for the people with Absalom continually increased in number.
verses.textEnNlt: While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel, one of David’s counselors who lived in Giloh. Soon many others also joined Absalom, and the conspiracy gained momentum.
verses.textEnNasb: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong, for the people continually increased with Absalom.
verses.textEn: While Absalom was offering sacrifices, he also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from Giloh, his hometown. And so the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept on increasing.

verses.textZh: 有一个报信的人来见大卫说："以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 有一个报信的人来见大卫说："以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 有人报告大卫说：「以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了！」
verses.textEnNiv: A messenger came and told David, "The hearts of the people of Israel are with Absalom."
verses.textEnEsv: And a messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom."
verses.textEnNkjv: Now a messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom."
verses.textEnNlt: A messenger soon arrived in Jerusalem to tell David, "All Israel has joined Absalom in a conspiracy against you!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then a messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the people of Israel are with Absalom."
verses.textEn: A messenger came and told David, "The hearts of the people of Israel are with Absalom."

verses.textZh: 大卫就对所有在耶路撒冷与他在一起的臣仆说："我们要起来逃走，不然我们就不能逃避押沙龙的面了，要赶快离开，恐怕他迅速赶上我们，使灾难临到我们身上，用刀击杀全城的人。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫就对所有在耶路撒冷与他在一起的臣仆说："我们要起来逃走，不然我们就不能逃避押沙龙的面了，要赶快离开，恐怕他迅速赶上我们，使灾难临到我们身上，用刀击杀全城的人。"
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫就对耶路撒冷跟随他的臣仆说：「我们要起来逃走，不然都不能躲避押沙龙了；要速速地去，恐怕他忽然来到，加害于我们，用刀杀尽合城的人。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, "Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us and bring ruin on us and put the city to the sword."
verses.textEnEsv: Then David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee, or else there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Go quickly, lest he overtake us quickly and bring down ruin on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.textEnNkjv: So David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, "Arise, and let us flee, or we shall not escape from Absalom. Make haste to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly and bring disaster upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.textEnNlt: "Then we must flee at once, or it will be too late!" David urged his men. "Hurry! If we get out of the city before Absalom arrives, both we and the city of Jerusalem will be spared from disaster."
verses.textEnNasb: So David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Arise and let’s flee, for otherwise none of us will escape from Absalom. Go quickly, or he will hurry and overtake us, and bring disaster on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.textEn: Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, "Come! We must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. We must leave immediately, or he will move quickly to overtake us and bring ruin on us and put the city to the sword."

verses.textZh: 王的臣仆对王说："我主我王决定的一切，仆人都必遵行。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王的臣仆对王说："我主我王决定的一切，仆人都必遵行。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王的臣仆对王说：「我主我王所定的，仆人都愿遵行。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king’s officials answered him, "Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king’s servants said to the king, "Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king decides."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king’s servants said to the king, "We are your servants, readytodo whatever my lord the king commands."
verses.textEnNlt: "We are with you," his advisers replied. "Do what you think is best."
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king’s servants said to the king, "Behold, your servants will do whatever my lord the king chooses."
verses.textEn: The king’s officials answered him, "Your servants are ready to do whatever our lord the king chooses."

verses.textZh: 于是王出走了，他的全家都跟在他的后头，却留下十个妃嫔看守王宫。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是王出走了，他的全家都跟在他的后头，却留下十个妃嫔看守王宫。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是王带着全家的人出去了，但留下十个妃嫔看守宫殿。
verses.textEnNiv: The king set out, with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace.
verses.textEnEsv: So the king went out, and all his household after him. And the king left ten concubines to keep the house.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king went out with all his household after him. But the king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.
verses.textEnNlt: So the king and all his household set out at once. He left no one behind except ten of his concubines to look after the palace.
verses.textEnNasb: So the king left, and all his household with him; but the king left ten concubines behind to take care of the house.
verses.textEn: The king set out, with his entire household following him; but he left ten concubines to take care of the palace.

verses.textZh: 王出发了，众人都跟在他的脚后；他们在伯．墨哈停下来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王出发了，众人都跟在他的脚后；他们在伯．墨哈停下来。
verses.textZhCuv: 王出去，众民都跟随他，到伯‧墨哈，就住下了。
verses.textEnNiv: So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at the edge of the city.
verses.textEnEsv: And the king went out, and all the people after him. And they halted at the last house.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king went out with all the people after him, and stopped at the outskirts.
verses.textEnNlt: The king and all his people set out on foot, pausing at the last house
verses.textEnNasb: The king left, and all the people with him, and they stopped at the last house.
verses.textEn: So the king set out, with all the people following him, and they halted at the edge of the city.

verses.textZh: 王所有的臣仆都从王的身边走过去，所有的基利提人、比利提人和迦特人，就是从迦特来跟从王的六百人，都从王面前走过去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王所有的臣仆都从王的身边走过去，所有的基利提人、比利提人和迦特人，就是从迦特来跟从王的六百人，都从王面前走过去。
verses.textZhCuv: 王的臣仆都在他面前过去。基利提人、比利提人，就是从迦特跟随王来的六百人，也都在他面前过去。
verses.textEnNiv: All his men marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites; and all the six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched before the king.
verses.textEnEsv: And all his servants passed by him, and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath, passed on before the king.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then all his servants passed before him; and all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had followed him from Gath, passed before the king.
verses.textEnNlt: to let all the king’s men move past to lead the way. There were 600 men from Gath who had come with David, along with the king’s bodyguard.
verses.textEnNasb: Now all of his servants passed by beside him, and all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come with him from Gath, passed by before the king.
verses.textEn: All his men marched past him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites; and all the six hundred Gittites who had accompanied him from Gath marched before the king.

verses.textZh: 王对迦特人以太说："你为甚么也与我们一同走呢？回去留在新王那里吧！因为你是个外族人，是个远离自己家乡逃到这里来的人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对迦特人以太说："你为甚么也与我们一同走呢？回去留在新王那里吧！因为你是个外族人，是个远离自己家乡逃到这里来的人。
verses.textZhCuv: 王对迦特人以太说：「你是外邦逃来的人，为什么与我们同去呢？你可以回去与新王同住，或者回你本地去吧！
verses.textEnNiv: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also go with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your home.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why are you also going with us? Return and remain with the king. For you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.
verses.textEnNlt: Then the king turned and said to Ittai, a leader of the men from Gath, "Why are you coming with us? Go on back to King Absalom, for you are a guest in Israel, a foreigner in exile.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you go with us too? Return and stay with your king, since you are a foreigner and an exile as well; return to your own place.
verses.textEn: The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with King Absalom. You are a foreigner, an exile from your homeland.

verses.textZh: 你昨天才来，我怎可以今天就让你与我们一同流浪呢？现在我还不知道我要到哪里去。你回去吧！带着你的兄弟一同回去吧！愿耶和华的 慈爱和信实与你同在。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 你昨天才来，我怎可以今天就让你与我们一同流浪呢？现在我还不知道我要到哪里去。你回去吧！带着你的兄弟一同回去吧！愿耶和华的 慈爱和信实与你同在。"
verses.textZhCuv: 你来的日子不多，我今日怎好叫你与我们一同飘流、没有一定的住处呢？你不如带你的弟兄回去吧！愿耶和华用慈爱诚实待你。」
verses.textEnNiv: You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your people with you. May the Lord show you kindness and faithfulness."
verses.textEnEsv: You came only yesterday, and shall I today make you wander about with us, since I go I know not where? Go back and take your brothers with you, and may the Lord show steadfast love and faithfulness to you."
verses.textEnNkjv: In fact, you came only yesterday. Should I make you wander up and down with us today, since I go I know not where? Return, and take your brethren back. Mercy and truth be with you."
verses.textEnNlt: You arrived only recently, and should I force you today to wander with us? I don’t even know where we will go. Go on back and take your kinsmen with you, and may the Lord show you his unfailing love and faithfulness. "
verses.textEnNasb: You came only yesterday, so should I make you wander with us today, while I go wherever I go? Return and take your brothers back; mercy and truth be with you."
verses.textEn: You came only yesterday. And today shall I make you wander about with us, when I do not know where I am going? Go back, and take your people with you. May the Lord show you kindness and faithfulness."

verses.textZh: 以太回答王说："我指着永活的耶和华，在我主我王面前起誓，无论我主我王在甚么地方，或生或死，你仆人也必在那里。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 以太回答王说："我指着永活的耶和华，在我主我王面前起誓，无论我主我王在甚么地方，或生或死，你仆人也必在那里。"
verses.textZhCuv: 以太对王说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，又敢在王面前起誓：无论生死，王在哪里，仆人也必在那里。」
verses.textEnNiv: But Ittai replied to the king, "As surely as the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be."
verses.textEnEsv: But Ittai answered the king, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether for death or for life, there also will your servant be."
verses.textEnNkjv: But Ittai answered the king and said, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in whatever place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also your servant will be."
verses.textEnNlt: But Ittai said to the king, "I vow by the Lord and by your own life that I will go wherever my lord the king goes, no matter what happens—whether it means life or death."
verses.textEnNasb: But Ittai answered the king and said, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether for death or for life, there assuredly shall your servant be!"
verses.textEn: But Ittai replied to the king, "As surely as the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be."

verses.textZh: 大卫对以太说："你可以去，向前走吧！"迦特人以太就带着所有属他的人，和与他在一起的妇人孩子都向前走。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫对以太说："你可以去，向前走吧！"迦特人以太就带着所有属他的人，和与他在一起的妇人孩子都向前走。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫对以太说：「你前去过河吧！」于是迦特人以太带着跟随他的人和所有的妇人孩子，就都过去了。
verses.textEnNiv: David said to Ittai, "Go ahead, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and the families that were with him.
verses.textEnEsv: And David said to Ittai, "Go then, pass on." So Ittai the Gittite passed on with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
verses.textEnNkjv: So David said to Ittai, "Go, and cross over." Then Ittai the Gittite and all his men and all the little ones who were with him crossed over.
verses.textEnNlt: David replied, "All right, come with us." So Ittai and all his men and their families went along.
verses.textEnNasb: Then David said to Ittai, "Go and cross over the brook Kidron." So Ittai the Gittite crossed over with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
verses.textEn: David said to Ittai, "Go ahead, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and the families that were with him.

verses.textZh: 众人向前走的时候，遍地的人都放声大哭；王过了汲沦溪，众人就都走上通往旷野去的路。
verses.textZhCnvs: 众人向前走的时候，遍地的人都放声大哭；王过了汲沦溪，众人就都走上通往旷野去的路。
verses.textZhCuv: 本地的人都放声大哭。众民尽都过去，王也过了汲沦溪；众民往旷野去了。
verses.textEnNiv: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness.
verses.textEnEsv: And all the land wept aloud as all the people passed by, and the king crossed the brook Kidron, and all the people passed on toward the wilderness.
verses.textEnNkjv: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people crossed over. The king himself also crossed over the Brook Kidron, and all the people crossed over toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.textEnNlt: Everyone cried loudly as the king and his followers passed by. They crossed the Kidron Valley and then went out toward the wilderness.
verses.textEnNasb: While all the country was weeping with a loud voice, all the people were crossing over. The king was also crossing over the brook Kidron, and all the people were crossing over toward the way of the wilderness.
verses.textEn: The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king also crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness.

verses.textZh: 看哪！撒督也来了，所有抬神约柜的利未人都与他在一起。他们把神的约柜放下。亚比亚他上来，直到从城里出来的众人都走过去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 看哪！撒督也来了，所有抬神约柜的利未人都与他在一起。他们把神的约柜放下。亚比亚他上来，直到从城里出来的众人都走过去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 撒督和抬神约柜的利未人也一同来了，将神的约柜放下。亚比亚他上来，等着众民从城里出来过去。
verses.textEnNiv: Zadok was there, too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.
verses.textEnEsv: And Abiathar came up, and behold, Zadok came also with all the Levites, bearing the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God until the people had all passed out of the city.
verses.textEnNkjv: There was Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished crossing over from the city.
verses.textEnNlt: Zadok and all the Levites also came along, carrying the Ark of the Covenant of God. They set down the Ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until everyone had passed out of the city.
verses.textEnNasb: Now behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar came up until all the people had finished crossing over from the city.
verses.textEn: Zadok was there, too, and all the Levites who were with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.

verses.textZh: 王对撒督说："把神的约柜抬回城里去吧！我若是在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来再看到约柜和他安居的地方。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对撒督说："把神的约柜抬回城里去吧！我若是在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来再看到约柜和他安居的地方。
verses.textZhCuv: 王对撒督说：「你将神的约柜抬回城去。我若在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来，再见约柜和他的居所。
verses.textEnNiv: Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the Lord ’s eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord , he will bring me back and let me see both it and his dwelling place.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, He will bring me back and show me both it and His dwelling place.
verses.textEnNlt: Then the king instructed Zadok to take the Ark of God back into the city. "If the Lord sees fit," David said, "he will bring me back to see the Ark and the Tabernacle again.
verses.textEnNasb: And the king said to Zadok, "Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the sight of the Lord, then He will bring me back and show me both it and His habitation.
verses.textEn: Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the Lord ’s eyes, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place again.

verses.textZh: 他若是说：‘我不喜悦你。’看哪！我就在这里，他看怎样好，就怎样对待我吧！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 他若是说：‘我不喜悦你。’看哪！我就在这里，他看怎样好，就怎样对待我吧！"
verses.textZhCuv: 倘若他说：『我不喜悦你』，看哪，我在这里，愿他凭自己的意旨待我！」
verses.textEnNiv: But if he says, ‘I am not pleased with you,’ then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him."
verses.textEnEsv: But if he says, ‘I have no pleasure in you,’ behold, here I am, let him do to me what seems good to him."
verses.textEnNkjv: But if He says thus: ‘I have no delight in you,’ here I am, let Him do to me as seems good to Him."
verses.textEnNlt: But if he is through with me, then let him do what seems best to him."
verses.textEnNasb: But if He says this: ‘I have no delight in you,’ then here I am, let Him do to me as seems good to Him."
verses.textEn: But if he says, ‘I am not pleased with you,’ then I am ready; let him do to me whatever seems good to him."

verses.textZh: 王又对撒督祭司说："你不是先见吗？平平安安地回到城里去吧！你的儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单要与你一同回去。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王又对撒督祭司说："你不是先见吗？平平安安地回到城里去吧！你的儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单要与你一同回去。
verses.textZhCuv: 王又对祭司撒督说：「你不是先见吗？你可以安然回城；你儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单都可以与你同去。
verses.textEnNiv: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Do you understand? Go back to the city with my blessing. Take your son Ahimaaz with you, and also Abiathar’s son Jonathan. You and Abiathar return with your two sons.
verses.textEnEsv: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Go back to the city in peace, with your two sons, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.textEnNkjv: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.textEnNlt: The king also told Zadok the priest, "Look, here is my plan. You and Abiathar should return quietly to the city with your son Ahimaaz and Abiathar’s son Jonathan.
verses.textEnNasb: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
verses.textEn: The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Do you understand? Go back to the city with my blessing. Take your son Ahimaaz with you, and also Abiathar’s son Jonathan. You and Abiathar return with your two sons.

verses.textZh: 我会在旷野的渡口那里等候，直到我接到从你们那里来的消息。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我会在旷野的渡口那里等候，直到我接到从你们那里来的消息。"
verses.textZhCuv: 我在旷野的渡口那里等你们报信给我。」
verses.textEnNiv: I will wait at the fords in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.textEnEsv: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.textEnNkjv: See, I will wait in the plains of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.textEnNlt: I will stop at the shallows of the Jordan River and wait there for a report from you."
verses.textEnNasb: See, I am going to wait at the river crossing places of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
verses.textEn: I will wait at the fords in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."

verses.textZh: 于是撒督和亚比亚他把神的约柜抬回耶路撒冷去，并且住在那里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是撒督和亚比亚他把神的约柜抬回耶路撒冷去，并且住在那里。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是撒督和亚比亚他将神的约柜抬回耶路撒冷，他们就住在那里。
verses.textEnNiv: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.
verses.textEnEsv: So Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem. And they remained there.
verses.textEnNlt: So Zadok and Abiathar took the Ark of God back to the city and stayed there.
verses.textEnNasb: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and remained there.
verses.textEn: So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.

verses.textZh: 大卫走上橄榄山；他蒙着头，赤着脚，一边上，一边哭，所有与他在一起的人民也都蒙着头，一边上，一边哭。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫走上橄榄山；他蒙着头，赤着脚，一边上，一边哭，所有与他在一起的人民也都蒙着头，一边上，一边哭。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫蒙头赤脚上橄榄山，一面上一面哭。跟随他的人也都蒙头哭着上去；
verses.textEnNiv: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and were weeping as they went up.
verses.textEnEsv: But David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, barefoot and with his head covered. And all the people who were with him covered their heads, and they went up, weeping as they went.
verses.textEnNkjv: So David went up by the Ascent of the Mountof Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered and went barefoot. And all the people who were with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went up.
verses.textEnNlt: David walked up the road to the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went. His head was covered and his feet were bare as a sign of mourning. And the people who were with him covered their heads and wept as they climbed the hill.
verses.textEnNasb: And David was going up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, and his head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. Then all the people who were with him each covered his own head, and they were going up, weeping as they went.
verses.textEn: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went; his head was covered and he was barefoot. All the people with him covered their heads too and were weeping as they went up.

verses.textZh: 有人告诉大卫说："亚希多弗也在押沙龙的叛党之中。"大卫祷告说："耶和华啊，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 有人告诉大卫说："亚希多弗也在押沙龙的叛党之中。"大卫祷告说："耶和华啊，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙。"
verses.textZhCuv: 有人告诉大卫说：「亚希多弗也在叛党之中，随从押沙龙。」大卫祷告说：「耶和华啊，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙！」
verses.textEnNiv: Now David had been told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." So David prayed, " Lord , turn Ahithophel’s counsel into foolishness."
verses.textEnEsv: And it was told David, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O Lord , please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then someone told David, saying, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "O Lord, I pray, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!"
verses.textEnNlt: When someone told David that his adviser Ahithophel was now backing Absalom, David prayed, "O Lord , let Ahithophel give Absalom foolish advice!"
verses.textEnNasb: Now someone informed David, saying, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." And David said, "Lord, please make the advice of Ahithophel foolish."
verses.textEn: Now David had been told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." So David prayed, " Lord , turn Ahithophel’s counsel into foolishness."

verses.textZh: 大卫到了山顶，就是人敬拜神的地方。看哪！有亚基人户筛衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘，在那里迎接他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫到了山顶，就是人敬拜神的地方。看哪！有亚基人户筛衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘，在那里迎接他。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫到了山顶、敬拜神的地方，见亚基人户筛，衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘来迎接他。
verses.textEnNiv: When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.
verses.textEnEsv: While David was coming to the summit, where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat torn and dirt on his head.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now it happened when David had come to the top ofthemountain, where he worshiped God—there was Hushai the Archite coming to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
verses.textEnNlt: When David reached the summit of the Mount of Olives where people worshiped God, Hushai the Arkite was waiting there for him. Hushai had torn his clothing and put dirt on his head as a sign of mourning.
verses.textEnNasb: It happened as David was coming to the summit, where God was worshiped, that behold, Hushai the Archite met him with his coat torn, and dust on his head.
verses.textEn: When David arrived at the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.

verses.textZh: 大卫对他说："你若是与我同去；必成为我的累赘。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫对他说："你若是与我同去；必成为我的累赘。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫对他说：「你若与我同去，必累赘我；
verses.textEnNiv: David said to him, "If you go with me, you will be a burden to me.
verses.textEnEsv: David said to him, "If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
verses.textEnNkjv: David said to him, "If you go on with me, then you will become a burden to me.
verses.textEnNlt: But David told him, "If you go with me, you will only be a burden.
verses.textEnNasb: And David said to him, "If you go over with me, then you will become a burden to me.
verses.textEn: David said to him, "If you go with me, you will be a burden to me.

verses.textZh: 如果你回到城里去，对押沙龙说：‘王啊！我愿作你的仆人，以前我作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。’这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。
verses.textZhCnvs: 如果你回到城里去，对押沙龙说：‘王啊！我愿作你的仆人，以前我作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。’这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。
verses.textZhCuv: 你若回城去，对押沙龙说：『王啊，我愿作你的仆人；我向来作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。』这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。
verses.textEnNiv: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘Your Majesty, I will be your servant; I was your father’s servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,’ then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel’s advice.
verses.textEnEsv: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king; as I have been your father’s servant in time past, so now I will be your servant,’ then you will defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.textEnNkjv: But if you return to the city, and say to Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father’s servant previously, so I will now also be your servant,’ then you may defeat the counsel of Ahithophel for me.
verses.textEnNlt: Return to Jerusalem and tell Absalom, ‘I will now be your adviser, O king, just as I was your father’s adviser in the past.’ Then you can frustrate and counter Ahithophel’s advice.
verses.textEnNasb: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king; even as I was your father’s servant in time past, so now I will also be your servant,’ then you can foil the advice of Ahithophel for me.
verses.textEn: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘Your Majesty, I will be your servant; I was your father’s servant in the past, but now I will be your servant,’ then you can help me by frustrating Ahithophel’s advice.

verses.textZh: 撒督祭司和亚比亚他不是都在那里与你在一起吗？你在王宫里听见的话，都要告诉撒督祭司和亚比亚他。
verses.textZhCnvs: 撒督祭司和亚比亚他不是都在那里与你在一起吗？你在王宫里听见的话，都要告诉撒督祭司和亚比亚他。
verses.textZhCuv: 祭司撒督和亚比亚他岂不都在那里吗？你在王宫里听见什么，就要告诉祭司撒督和亚比亚他。
verses.textEnNiv: Won’t the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them anything you hear in the king’s palace.
verses.textEnEsv: Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? So whatever you hear from the king’s house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.textEnNkjv: And do you not have Zadok and Abiathar the priests with you there? Therefore it will be that whatever you hear from the king’s house, you shall tell to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.textEnNlt: Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, will be there. Tell them about the plans being made in the king’s palace,
verses.textEnNasb: Are Zadok and Abiathar the priests not with you there? So it shall be that whatever you hear from the king’s house, you shall report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.textEn: Won’t the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Tell them anything you hear in the king’s palace.

verses.textZh: 看哪！还有他们的两个儿子和他们在那里，就是撒督的儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单。你们听见的一切，可以托他们来告诉我。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 看哪！还有他们的两个儿子和他们在那里，就是撒督的儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单。你们听见的一切，可以托他们来告诉我。"
verses.textZhCuv: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯，亚比亚他的儿子约拿单，也都在那里。凡你们所听见的可以托这二人来报告我。」
verses.textEnNiv: Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear."
verses.textEnEsv: Behold, their two sons are with them there, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son, and by them you shall send to me everything you hear."
verses.textEnNkjv: Indeed theyhave there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son; and by them you shall send me everything you hear."
verses.textEnNlt: and they will send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what is going on."
verses.textEnNasb: Behold their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son; and by them you shall send me everything that you hear."
verses.textEn: Their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with anything you hear."

verses.textZh: 于是大卫的朋友户筛进了城；押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是大卫的朋友户筛进了城；押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是，大卫的朋友户筛进了城；押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。
verses.textEnNiv: So Hushai, David’s confidant, arrived at Jerusalem as Absalom was entering the city.
verses.textEnEsv: So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city, just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: So Hushai, David’s friend, went into the city. And Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNlt: So David’s friend Hushai returned to Jerusalem, getting there just as Absalom arrived.
verses.textEnNasb: So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: So Hushai, David’s confidant, arrived at Jerusalem as Absalom was entering the city.

verses.textZh: 大卫刚越过山顶不远，就看见米非波设的仆人洗巴前来迎接他；又有一对预备好了的驴子，驴子身上驮着两百个饼，一百个葡萄干饼，一百个夏天的果饼和一皮袋酒。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫刚越过山顶不远，就看见米非波设的仆人洗巴前来迎接他；又有一对预备好了的驴子，驴子身上驮着两百个饼，一百个葡萄干饼，一百个夏天的果饼和一皮袋酒。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫刚过山顶，见米非波设的仆人洗巴拉着备好了的两匹驴，驴上驮着二百面饼，一百葡萄饼，一百个夏天的果饼，一皮袋酒来迎接他。
verses.textEnNiv: When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth, waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs and a skin of wine.
verses.textEnEsv: When David had passed a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of donkeys saddled, bearing two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred of summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
verses.textEnNkjv: When David was a little past the top ofthemountain, there was Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth, who met him with a couple of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
verses.textEnNlt: When David had gone a little beyond the summit of the Mount of Olives, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, was waiting there for him. He had two donkeys loaded with 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 bunches of summer fruit, and a wineskin full of wine.
verses.textEnNasb: Now when David had gone on a little beyond the summit, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a team of saddled donkeys, and on them were two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a jug of wine.
verses.textEn: When David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth, waiting to meet him. He had a string of donkeys saddled and loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs and a skin of wine.

verses.textZh: 王问洗巴："你为甚么带这些东西来？"洗巴回答："驴子是给王的家眷骑的，饼和夏天的果饼是给年轻人吃的，酒是给在旷野里疲乏的人喝的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王问洗巴："你为甚么带这些东西来？"洗巴回答："驴子是给王的家眷骑的，饼和夏天的果饼是给年轻人吃的，酒是给在旷野里疲乏的人喝的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王问洗巴说：「你带这些来是什么意思呢？」洗巴说：「驴是给王的家眷骑的；面饼和夏天的果饼是给少年人吃的；酒是给在旷野疲乏人喝的。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king asked Ziba, "Why have you brought these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said to Ziba, "Why have you brought these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who faint in the wilderness to drink."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said to Ziba, "What do you mean to do with these?" So Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who are faint in the wilderness to drink."
verses.textEnNlt: "What are these for?" the king asked Ziba. Ziba replied, "The donkeys are for the king’s people to ride on, and the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat. The wine is for those who become exhausted in the wilderness."
verses.textEnNasb: And the king said to Ziba, "Why do you have these?" And Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine, for whoever is weary in the wilderness to drink."
verses.textEn: The king asked Ziba, "Why have you brought these?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and fruit are for the men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness."

verses.textZh: 王又问："你主人的孙子米非波设在哪里？"洗巴回答王说："唉！他还留在耶路撒冷，因为他心里想：‘今日以色列家会把我祖父扫罗的王国归还给我。’"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王又问："你主人的孙子米非波设在哪里？"洗巴回答王说："唉！他还留在耶路撒冷，因为他心里想：‘今日以色列家会把我祖父扫罗的王国归还给我。’"
verses.textZhCuv: 王问说：「你主人的儿子在哪里呢？」洗巴回答王说：「他仍在耶路撒冷，因他说：『以色列人今日必将我父的国归还我。』」
verses.textEnNiv: The king then asked, "Where is your master’s grandson?" Ziba said to him, "He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, ‘Today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather’s kingdom.’ "
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said, "And where is your master’s son?" Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he remains in Jerusalem, for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will give me back the kingdom of my father.’"
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king said, "And where is your master’s son?" And Ziba said to the king, "Indeed he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore the kingdom of my father to me.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: "And where is Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson?" the king asked him. "He stayed in Jerusalem," Ziba replied. "He said, ‘Today I will get back the kingdom of my grandfather Saul.’"
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king said, "And where is your master’s son?" And Ziba said to the king, "Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore the kingdom of my father to me.’ "
verses.textEn: The king then asked, "Where is your master’s grandson?" Ziba said to him, "He is staying in Jerusalem, because he thinks, ‘Today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather’s kingdom.’ "

verses.textZh: 王对洗巴说："看哪！凡属米非波设所有的，都归给你了。"洗巴说："我叩拜我主我王，愿我在你眼前蒙恩！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对洗巴说："看哪！凡属米非波设所有的，都归给你了。"洗巴说："我叩拜我主我王，愿我在你眼前蒙恩！"
verses.textZhCuv: 王对洗巴说：「凡属米非波设的都归你了。」洗巴说：「我叩拜我主我王，愿我在你眼前蒙恩。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then the king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." "I humbly bow," Ziba said. "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." And Ziba said, "I pay homage; let me ever find favor in your sight, my lord the king."
verses.textEnNkjv: So the king said to Ziba, "Here, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I humbly bow before you, that I may find favor in your sight, my lord, O king!"
verses.textEnNlt: "In that case," the king told Ziba, "I give you everything Mephibosheth owns." "I bow before you," Ziba replied. "May I always be pleasing to you, my lord the king."
verses.textEnNasb: So the king said to Ziba, "Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "I prostrate myself; may I find favor in your sight, my lord, the king!"
verses.textEn: Then the king said to Ziba, "All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." "I humbly bow," Ziba said. "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."

verses.textZh: 大卫王来到巴户琳的时候，忽然有一人从那里出来，他是属扫罗家族的，名叫示每，是基拉的儿子。他一边出来，一边咒骂；
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫王来到巴户琳的时候，忽然有一人从那里出来，他是属扫罗家族的，名叫示每，是基拉的儿子。他一边出来，一边咒骂；
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫王到了巴户琳，见有一个人出来，是扫罗族基拉的儿子，名叫示每。他一面走一面咒骂，
verses.textEnNiv: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the same clan as Saul’s family came out from there. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he cursed as he came out.
verses.textEnEsv: When King David came to Bahurim, there came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera, and as he came he cursed continually.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now when King David came to Bahurim, there was a man from the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei the son of Gera, coming from there. He came out, cursing continuously as he came.
verses.textEnNlt: As King David came to Bahurim, a man came out of the village cursing them. It was Shimei son of Gera, from the same clan as Saul’s family.
