verses.textEnEsv: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself the pillar that is in the King’s Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Absalom’s monument to this day.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up a pillar for himself, which is in the King’s Valley. For he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar after his own name. And to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
verses.textEnNlt: During his lifetime, Absalom had built a monument to himself in the King’s Valley, for he said, "I have no son to carry on my name." He named the monument after himself, and it is known as Absalom’s Monument to this day.
verses.textEnNasb: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself a memorial stone, which is in the King’s Valley, for he said, "I have no son to continue my name." So he named the memorial stone after his own name, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day.
verses.textEn: During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and erected it in the King’s Valley as a monument to himself, for he thought, "I have no son to carry on the memory of my name." He named the pillar after himself, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day.

verses.textZh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说："让我跑去，把这好消息向王报告，就是耶和华已经把他从仇敌的手中拯救出来了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说："让我跑去，把这好消息向王报告，就是耶和华已经把他从仇敌的手中拯救出来了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说：「容我跑去，将耶和华向仇敌给王报仇的信息报与王知。」
verses.textEnNiv: Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and take the news to the king that the Lord has vindicated him by delivering him from the hand of his enemies."
verses.textEnEsv: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Let me run and carry news to the king that the Lord has delivered him from the hand of his enemies."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Let me run now and take the news to the king, how the Lord has avenged him of his enemies."
verses.textEnNlt: Then Zadok’s son Ahimaaz said, "Let me run to the king with the good news that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies."
verses.textEnNasb: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Please let me run and bring the king news that the Lord has freed him from the hand of his enemies!"
verses.textEn: Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and take the news to the king that the Lord has vindicated him by delivering him from the hand of his enemies."

verses.textZh: 约押对他说："你今天不可去报消息，改天才可以去报。你今天不可去报消息，因为王的儿子死了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 约押对他说："你今天不可去报消息，改天才可以去报。你今天不可去报消息，因为王的儿子死了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 约押对他说：「你今日不可去报信，改日可以报信；因为今日王的儿子死了，所以你不可去报信。」
verses.textEnNiv: "You are not the one to take the news today," Joab told him. "You may take the news another time, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead."
verses.textEnEsv: And Joab said to him, "You are not to carry news today. You may carry news another day, but today you shall carry no news, because the king’s son is dead."
verses.textEnNkjv: And Joab said to him, "You shall not take the news this day, for you shall take the news another day. But today you shall take no news, because the king’s son is dead."
verses.textEnNlt: "No," Joab told him, "it wouldn’t be good news to the king that his son is dead. You can be my messenger another time, but not today."
verses.textEnNasb: But Joab said to him, "You are not the man to bring news this day, but you shall bring news another day; however, you shall bring no news this day, because the king’s son is dead."
verses.textEn: "You are not the one to take the news today," Joab told him. "You may take the news another time, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead."

verses.textZh: 于是约押对一个古实人说："你去把你所看见的告诉王吧！"那古实人叩拜了约押，就跑去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是约押对一个古实人说："你去把你所看见的告诉王吧！"那古实人叩拜了约押，就跑去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 约押对古示人说：「你去将你所看见的告诉王。」古示人在约押面前下拜，就跑去了。
verses.textEnNiv: Then Joab said to a Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed down before Joab and ran off.
verses.textEnEsv: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed before Joab, and ran.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." So the Cushite bowed himself to Joab and ran.
verses.textEnNlt: Then Joab said to a man from Ethiopia, "Go tell the king what you have seen." The man bowed and ran off.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." So the Cushite bowed to Joab and ran.
verses.textEn: Then Joab said to a Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed down before Joab and ran off.

verses.textZh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说："不管怎样，请让我也跟着那古实人跑去。"约押说："你为甚么要跑去呢？我儿，你是不会得到报消息的赏赐的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说："不管怎样，请让我也跟着那古实人跑去。"约押说："你为甚么要跑去呢？我儿，你是不会得到报消息的赏赐的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说：「无论怎样，求你容我随着古示人跑去。」约押说：「我儿，你报这信息，既不得赏赐，何必要跑去呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: Ahimaaz son of Zadok again said to Joab, "Come what may, please let me run behind the Cushite." But Joab replied, "My son, why do you want to go? You don’t have any news that will bring you a reward."
verses.textEnEsv: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, let me also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why will you run, my son, seeing that you will have no reward for the news?"
verses.textEnNkjv: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said again to Joab, "But whatever happens, please let me also run after the Cushite." So Joab said, "Why will you run, my son, since you have no news ready?"
verses.textEnNlt: But Ahimaaz continued to plead with Joab, "Whatever happens, please let me go, too." "Why should you go, my son?" Joab replied. "There will be no reward for your news."
verses.textEnNasb: However, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said once more to Joab, "But whatever happens, please let me also run after the Cushite." And Joab said, "Why would you run, my son, since you will have no messenger’s reward for going?"
verses.textEn: Ahimaaz son of Zadok again said to Joab, "Come what may, please let me run behind the Cushite." But Joab replied, "My son, why do you want to go? You don’t have any news that will bring you a reward."

verses.textZh: "不管怎样，请让我跑去！"于是约押对他说："你跑去吧！"亚希玛斯就沿着约旦河大道跑去，赶过了那古实人。
verses.textZhCnvs: "不管怎样，请让我跑去！"于是约押对他说："你跑去吧！"亚希玛斯就沿着约旦河大道跑去，赶过了那古实人。
verses.textZhCuv: 他又说：「无论怎样，我要跑去。」约押说：「你跑去吧！」亚希玛斯就从平原往前跑，跑过古示人去了。
verses.textEnNiv: He said, "Come what may, I want to run." So Joab said, "Run!" Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
verses.textEnEsv: "Come what may," he said, "I will run." So he said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and outran the Cushite.
verses.textEnNkjv: "But whatever happens," hesaid, "let me run." So he said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain, and outran the Cushite.
verses.textEnNlt: "Yes, but let me go anyway," he begged. Joab finally said, "All right, go ahead." So Ahimaaz took the less demanding route by way of the plain and ran to Mahanaim ahead of the Ethiopian.
verses.textEnNasb: "But whatever happens," he said, "I will run." So he said to him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and passed by the Cushite.
verses.textEn: He said, "Come what may, I want to run." So Joab said, "Run!" Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.

verses.textZh: 那时，大卫正坐在内外城门中间的地方。守望的人上到城楼的平顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那时，大卫正坐在内外城门中间的地方。守望的人上到城楼的平顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫正坐在城瓮里。守望的人上城门楼的顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。
verses.textEnNiv: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates, the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.
verses.textEnEsv: Now David was sitting between the two gates, and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate by the wall, and when he lifted up his eyes and looked, he saw a man running alone.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now David was sitting between the two gates. And the watchman went up to the roof over the gate, to the wall, lifted his eyes and looked, and there was a man, running alone.
verses.textEnNlt: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates of the town, the watchman climbed to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked, he saw a lone man running toward them.
verses.textEnNasb: Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman went to the roof of the gate by the wall, and raised his eyes and looked; and behold, a man was running by himself.
verses.textEn: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates, the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked out, he saw a man running alone.

verses.textZh: 守望的人就喊叫，把这事告诉王；王说："他若是单独一人，必是来报好消息的。"那人越走越近了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 守望的人就喊叫，把这事告诉王；王说："他若是单独一人，必是来报好消息的。"那人越走越近了。
verses.textZhCuv: 守望的人就大声告诉王。王说：「他若独自来，必是报口信的。」那人跑得渐渐近了。
verses.textEnNiv: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, "If he is alone, he must have good news." And the runner came closer and closer.
verses.textEnEsv: The watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." And he drew nearer and nearer.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the watchman cried out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, thereis news in his mouth." And he came rapidly and drew near.
verses.textEnNlt: He shouted the news down to David, and the king replied, "If he is alone, he has news." As the messenger came closer,
verses.textEnNasb: So the watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, "If he is by himself there is good news in his mouth." And he came nearer and nearer.
verses.textEn: The watchman called out to the king and reported it. The king said, "If he is alone, he must have good news." And the runner came closer and closer.

verses.textZh: 后来，守望的人又看见另一个人跑来，就对守城门的人喊叫，说："看哪！又有一个人独自跑来！"王说："这也必是来报好消息的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 后来，守望的人又看见另一个人跑来，就对守城门的人喊叫，说："看哪！又有一个人独自跑来！"王说："这也必是来报好消息的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 守望的人又见一人跑来，就对守城门的人说：「又有一人独自跑来。」王说：「这也必是报信的。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then the watchman saw another runner, and he called down to the gatekeeper, "Look, another man running alone!" The king said, "He must be bringing good news, too."
verses.textEnEsv: The watchman saw another man running. And the watchman called to the gate and said, "See, another man running alone!" The king said, "He also brings news."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, "There is another man, running alone!" And the king said, "He also brings news."
verses.textEnNlt: the watchman saw another man running toward them. He shouted down, "Here comes another one!" The king replied, "He also will have news."
verses.textEnNasb: Then the watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, "Behold, another man is running by himself." And the king said, "This one also is bringing good news."
verses.textEn: Then the watchman saw another runner, and he called down to the gatekeeper, "Look, another man running alone!" The king said, "He must be bringing good news, too."

verses.textZh: 守望的人说："我看前头那人的跑法好象撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。"王说："他是个好人，必是带好消息来的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 守望的人说："我看前头那人的跑法好象撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。"王说："他是个好人，必是带好消息来的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 守望的人说：「我看前头人的跑法，好像撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。」王说：「他是个好人，必是报好信息。」
verses.textEnNiv: The watchman said, "It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He’s a good man," the king said. "He comes with good news."
verses.textEnEsv: The watchman said, "I think the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man and comes with good news."
verses.textEnNkjv: So the watchman said, "I think the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "He is a good man, and comes with good news."
verses.textEnNlt: "The first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok," the watchman said. "He is a good man and comes with good news," the king replied.
verses.textEnNasb: The watchman said, "I think the running form of the first one is like the running form of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "This is a good man, and he is coming with good news."
verses.textEn: The watchman said, "It seems to me that the first one runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He’s a good man," the king said. "He comes with good news."

verses.textZh: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫，说："平安！"就脸伏于地，叩拜王，说："耶和华你的神是应当称颂的，因为他已经把举手攻击我主我王的人交给你了！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫，说："平安！"就脸伏于地，叩拜王，说："耶和华你的神是应当称颂的，因为他已经把举手攻击我主我王的人交给你了！"
verses.textZhCuv: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫说：「平安了！」就在王面前脸伏于地叩拜，说：「耶和华－你的神是应当称颂的，因他已将那举手攻击我主我王的人交给王了。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise be to the Lord your God! He has delivered up those who lifted their hands against my lord the king."
verses.textEnEsv: Then Ahimaaz cried out to the king, "All is well." And he bowed before the king with his face to the earth and said, "Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who raised their hand against my lord the king."
verses.textEnNkjv: So Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "All is well!" Then he bowed down with his face to the earth before the king, and said, "Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who raised their hand against my lord the king!"
verses.textEnNlt: Then Ahimaaz cried out to the king, "Everything is all right!" He bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise to the Lord your God, who has handed over the rebels who dared to stand against my lord the king."
verses.textEnNasb: Then Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, " All is well." And he prostrated himself before the king with his face to the ground. And he said, "Blessed is the Lord your God, who has turned over the men who raised their hands against my lord the king."
verses.textEn: Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed down before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise be to the Lord your God! He has delivered up those who lifted their hands against my lord the king."

verses.textZh: 王问："那年轻人押沙龙平安不平安？"亚希玛斯回答："约押差派王的仆人，就是你的仆人我来的时候，我看见有大动乱，却不知道是甚么事。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王问："那年轻人押沙龙平安不平安？"亚希玛斯回答："约押差派王的仆人，就是你的仆人我来的时候，我看见有大动乱，却不知道是甚么事。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王问说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」亚希玛斯回答说：「约押打发王的仆人，那时仆人听见众民大声喧哗，却不知道是什么事。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "I saw great confusion just as Joab was about to send the king’s servant and me, your servant, but I don’t know what it was."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king’s servant, your servant, I saw a great commotion, but I do not know what it was."
verses.textEnNkjv: The king said, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king’s servant and me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I did not know what itwasabout."
verses.textEnNlt: "What about young Absalom?" the king demanded. "Is he all right?" Ahimaaz replied, "When Joab told me to come, there was a lot of commotion. But I didn’t know what was happening."
verses.textEnNasb: But the king said, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king’s servant, and your servant, I saw a great commotion, but I did not know what it was."
verses.textEn: The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "I saw great confusion just as Joab was about to send the king’s servant and me, your servant, but I don’t know what it was."

verses.textZh: 王说："你退到一旁，站在那里！"他就退到一旁，站在那里。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王说："你退到一旁，站在那里！"他就退到一旁，站在那里。
verses.textZhCuv: 王说：「你退去，站在旁边。」他就退去，站在旁边。
verses.textEnNiv: The king said, "Stand aside and wait here." So he stepped aside and stood there.
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." So he turned aside and stood still.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." So he turned aside and stood still.
verses.textEnNlt: "Wait here," the king told him. So Ahimaaz stepped aside.
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king said, "Turn aside and stand here." So he turned aside and stood still.
verses.textEn: The king said, "Stand aside and wait here." So he stepped aside and stood there.

verses.textZh: 那古实人也到了。他说："有好消息报给我主我王；今天耶和华已经救你脱离那些起来攻击你的人的手了！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 那古实人也到了。他说："有好消息报给我主我王；今天耶和华已经救你脱离那些起来攻击你的人的手了！"
verses.textZhCuv: 古示人也来到，说：「有信息报给我主我王！耶和华今日向一切兴起攻击你的人给你报仇了。」
verses.textEnNiv: Then the Cushite arrived and said, "My lord the king, hear the good news! The Lord has vindicated you today by delivering you from the hand of all who rose up against you."
verses.textEnEsv: And behold, the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "Good news for my lord the king! For the Lord has delivered you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you."
verses.textEnNkjv: Just then the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "There is good news, my lord the king! For the Lord has avenged you this day of all those who rose against you."
verses.textEnNlt: Then the man from Ethiopia arrived and said, "I have good news for my lord the king. Today the Lord has rescued you from all those who rebelled against you."
verses.textEnNasb: Then behold, the Cushite arrived, and the Cushite said, "Let my lord the king receive good news, for the Lord has freed you this day from the hand of all those who rose up against you."
verses.textEn: Then the Cushite arrived and said, "My lord the king, hear the good news! The Lord has vindicated you today by delivering you from the hand of all who rose up against you."

verses.textZh: 王问古实人："那年轻人押沙龙平安吗？"古实人回答："愿我主我王的仇敌和一切来攻击你、伤害你的人，都像那年轻人一样。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王问古实人："那年轻人押沙龙平安吗？"古实人回答："愿我主我王的仇敌和一切来攻击你、伤害你的人，都像那年轻人一样。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王问古示人说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」古示人回答说：「愿我主我王的仇敌，和一切兴起要杀害你的人，都与那少年人一样。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite replied, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up to harm you be like that young man."
verses.textEnEsv: The king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And the Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you for evil be like that young man."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said to the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" So the Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise against you to do harm, be like that young man!"
verses.textEnNlt: "What about young Absalom?" the king demanded. "Is he all right?" And the Ethiopian replied, "May all of your enemies, my lord the king, both now and in the future, share the fate of that young man!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" And the Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you for evil, be like that young man!"
verses.textEn: The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite replied, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up to harm you be like that young man."

verses.textZh: 王悲恸得全身发抖，就上城楼去哀哭。他一面走一面这样说："我儿押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿押沙龙啊！但愿我替你死。押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿啊！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王悲恸得全身发抖，就上城楼去哀哭。他一面走一面这样说："我儿押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿押沙龙啊！但愿我替你死。押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿啊！"
verses.textZhCuv: 王就心里伤恸，上城门楼去哀哭，一面走一面说：「我儿押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿押沙龙啊！我恨不得替你死，押沙龙啊，我儿！我儿！」
verses.textEnNiv: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he said: "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you—O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnEsv: And the king was deeply moved and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he went, he said, "O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king was deeply moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept. And as he went, he said thus: "O my son Absalom—my son, my son Absalom—if only I had died in your place! O Absalom my son, my son!"
verses.textEnNlt: The king was overcome with emotion. He went up to the room over the gateway and burst into tears. And as he went, he cried, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you! O Absalom, my son, my son."
verses.textEnNasb: Then the king trembled and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And this is what he said as he walked: "My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEn: The king was shaken. He went up to the room over the gateway and wept. As he went, he said: "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you—O Absalom, my son, my son!"

verses.textZh: 有人告诉约押："看哪！王正在为押沙龙悲哀哭泣。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 有人告诉约押："看哪！王正在为押沙龙悲哀哭泣。"
verses.textZhCuv: 有人告诉约押说：「王为押沙龙哭泣悲哀。」
verses.textEnNiv: Joab was told, "The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
verses.textEnEsv: It was told Joab, "Behold, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
verses.textEnNkjv: And Joab was told, "Behold, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
verses.textEnNlt: Word soon reached Joab that the king was weeping and mourning for Absalom.
verses.textEnNasb: Then it was reported to Joab, "Behold, the king is weeping and he mourns for Absalom."
verses.textEn: Joab was told, "The king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."

verses.textZh: 那一天，众人胜利的欢乐变成了悲哀，因为他们听说王为他的儿子伤痛。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那一天，众人胜利的欢乐变成了悲哀，因为他们听说王为他的儿子伤痛。
verses.textZhCuv: 众民听说王为他儿子忧愁，他们得胜的欢乐却变成悲哀。
verses.textEnNiv: And for the whole army the victory that day was turned into mourning, because on that day the troops heard it said, "The king is grieving for his son."
verses.textEnEsv: So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard that day, "The king is grieving for his son."
verses.textEnNkjv: So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people. For the people heard it said that day, "The king is grieved for his son."
verses.textEnNlt: As all the people heard of the king’s deep grief for his son, the joy of that day’s victory was turned into deep sadness.
verses.textEnNasb: So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, because the people heard it said that day, "The king is in mourning over his son."
verses.textEn: And for the whole army the victory that day was turned into mourning, because on that day the troops heard it said, "The king is grieving for his son."

verses.textZh: 那一天，众人偷偷进城，就像军人从战场上逃跑，羞愧地偷偷回来一样。
verses.textZhCnvs: 那一天，众人偷偷进城，就像军人从战场上逃跑，羞愧地偷偷回来一样。
verses.textZhCuv: 那日众民暗暗地进城，就如败阵逃跑、惭愧的民一般。
verses.textEnNiv: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.
verses.textEnEsv: And the people stole into the city that day as people steal in who are ashamed when they flee in battle.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the people stole back into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
verses.textEnNlt: They crept back into the town that day as though they were ashamed and had deserted in battle.
verses.textEnNasb: And the people entered the city surreptitiously that day, just as people who are humiliated surreptitiously flee in battle.
verses.textEn: The men stole into the city that day as men steal in who are ashamed when they flee from battle.

verses.textZh: 王蒙着脸，大声哀哭，说："我儿押沙龙啊！押沙龙，我儿，我儿啊！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王蒙着脸，大声哀哭，说："我儿押沙龙啊！押沙龙，我儿，我儿啊！"
verses.textZhCuv: 王蒙着脸，大声哭号说：「我儿押沙龙啊！押沙龙，我儿，我儿啊！」
verses.textEnNiv: The king covered his face and cried aloud, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnEsv: The king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, "O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnNkjv: But the king covered his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnNlt: The king covered his face with his hands and kept on crying, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEnNasb: And the king covered his face and cried out with a loud voice, "My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.textEn: The king covered his face and cried aloud, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"

verses.textZh: 约押进了屋子去见王，说："你所有的臣仆今天救了你的性命，和你儿女妻妾的性命，你今天却使他们满面羞愧；
verses.textZhCnvs: 约押进了屋子去见王，说："你所有的臣仆今天救了你的性命，和你儿女妻妾的性命，你今天却使他们满面羞愧；
verses.textZhCuv: 约押进去见王，说：「你今日使你一切仆人脸面惭愧了！他们今日救了你的性命和你儿女妻妾的性命，
verses.textEnNiv: Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, "Today you have humiliated all your men, who have just saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters and the lives of your wives and concubines.
verses.textEnEsv: Then Joab came into the house to the king and said, "You have today covered with shame the faces of all your servants, who have this day saved your life and the lives of your sons and your daughters and the lives of your wives and your concubines,
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Joab came into the house to the king, and said, "Today you have disgraced all your servants who today have saved your life, the lives of your sons and daughters, the lives of your wives and the lives of your concubines,
verses.textEnNlt: Then Joab went to the king’s room and said to him, "We saved your life today and the lives of your sons, your daughters, and your wives and concubines. Yet you act like this, making us feel ashamed of ourselves.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Joab came into the house to the king and said, "Today you have shamed all your servants, who have saved your life today and the lives of your sons and daughters, the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines,
verses.textEn: Then Joab went into the house to the king and said, "Today you have humiliated all your men, who have just saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters and the lives of your wives and concubines.

verses.textZh: 你爱那些恨你的，恨那些爱你的。因为你今天表明了你不重视将帅和臣仆；我今天才明白，如果押沙龙活着，我们大家都死去，你就欢喜了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 你爱那些恨你的，恨那些爱你的。因为你今天表明了你不重视将帅和臣仆；我今天才明白，如果押沙龙活着，我们大家都死去，你就欢喜了。
verses.textZhCuv: 你却爱那恨你的人，恨那爱你的人。你今日明明地不以将帅、仆人为念。我今日看明，若押沙龙活着，我们都死亡，你就喜悦了。
verses.textEnNiv: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that the commanders and their men mean nothing to you. I see that you would be pleased if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.
verses.textEnEsv: because you love those who hate you and hate those who love you. For you have made it clear today that commanders and servants are nothing to you, for today I know that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then you would be pleased.
verses.textEnNkjv: in that you love your enemies and hate your friends. For you have declared today that you regard neither princes nor servants; for today I perceive that if Absalom had lived and all of us had died today, then it would have pleased you well.
verses.textEnNlt: You seem to love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that your commanders and troops mean nothing to you. It seems that if Absalom had lived and all of us had died, you would be pleased.
verses.textEnNasb: by loving those who hate you, and by hating those who love you. For you have revealed today that commanders and servants are nothing to you; for I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then it would be right as far as you are concerned.
verses.textEn: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that the commanders and their men mean nothing to you. I see that you would be pleased if Absalom were alive today and all of us were dead.

verses.textZh: 现在请你起来，出去，说些安慰你仆人们的话。我指着耶和华起誓，如果你不出去，今夜就必没有一人留下来与你在一起。这祸患就比你从幼年到现在所遭受的一切祸患更厉害了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 现在请你起来，出去，说些安慰你仆人们的话。我指着耶和华起誓，如果你不出去，今夜就必没有一人留下来与你在一起。这祸患就比你从幼年到现在所遭受的一切祸患更厉害了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 现在你当出去，安慰你仆人的心。我指着耶和华起誓：你若不出去，今夜必无一人与你同在一处；这祸患就比你从幼年到如今所遭的更甚！」
verses.textEnNiv: Now go out and encourage your men. I swear by the Lord that if you don’t go out, not a man will be left with you by nightfall. This will be worse for you than all the calamities that have come on you from your youth till now."
verses.textEnEsv: Now therefore arise, go out and speak kindly to your servants, for I swear by the Lord , if you do not go, not a man will stay with you this night, and this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now."
verses.textEnNkjv: Now therefore, arise, go out and speak comfort to your servants. For I swear by the Lord, if you do not go out, not one will stay with you this night. And that will be worse for you than all the evil that has befallen you from your youth until now."
verses.textEnNlt: Now go out there and congratulate your troops, for I swear by the Lord that if you don’t go out, not a single one of them will remain here tonight. Then you will be worse off than ever before."
verses.textEnNasb: Now therefore arise, go out and speak kindly to your servants, for I swear by the Lord, if you do not go out, no man will stay the night with you, and this will be worse for you than all the misfortune that has happened to you from your youth until now!"
verses.textEn: Now go out and encourage your men. I swear by the Lord that if you don’t go out, not a man will be left with you by nightfall. This will be worse for you than all the calamities that have come on you from your youth till now."

verses.textZh: 于是王起来，坐在城门口。有人告诉众民说："看哪！王坐在城门口。"于是众人都来到王的面前。 以色列人已经逃跑，各回自己的家去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是王起来，坐在城门口。有人告诉众民说："看哪！王坐在城门口。"于是众人都来到王的面前。 以色列人已经逃跑，各回自己的家去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是王起来，坐在城门口。众民听说王坐在城门口，就都到王面前。 以色列人已经逃跑，各回各家去了。
verses.textEnNiv: So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the men were told, "The king is sitting in the gateway," they all came before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled to their homes.
verses.textEnEsv: Then the king arose and took his seat in the gate. And the people were all told, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled every man to his own home.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king arose and sat in the gate. And they told all the people, saying, "There is the king, sitting in the gate." So all the people came before the king. For everyone of Israel had fled to his tent.
verses.textEnNlt: So the king went out and took his seat at the town gate, and as the news spread throughout the town that he was there, everyone went to him. Meanwhile, the Israelites who had supported Absalom fled to their homes.
verses.textEnNasb: So the king got up and sat at the gate. When they told all the people, saying, "Behold, the king is sitting at the gate," then all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, each to his tent.
verses.textEn: So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the men were told, "The king is sitting in the gateway," they all came before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled to their homes.

verses.textZh: 以色列众支派的人都纷纷议论，说："王曾经拯救我们脱离仇敌的手，又救了我们脱离非利士人的手，现在他却躲避押沙龙，离开这地逃走了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 以色列众支派的人都纷纷议论，说："王曾经拯救我们脱离仇敌的手，又救了我们脱离非利士人的手，现在他却躲避押沙龙，离开这地逃走了。
verses.textZhCuv: 以色列众支派的人纷纷议论说：「王曾救我们脱离仇敌的手，又救我们脱离非利士人的手，现在他躲避押沙龙逃走了。
verses.textEnNiv: Throughout the tribes of Israel, all the people were arguing among themselves, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he is the one who rescued us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the country to escape from Absalom;
verses.textEnEsv: And all the people were arguing throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies and saved us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now all the people were in a dispute throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king saved us from the hand of our enemies, he delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.
verses.textEnNlt: And throughout all the tribes of Israel there was much discussion and argument going on. The people were saying, "The king rescued us from our enemies and saved us from the Philistines, but Absalom chased him out of the country.
verses.textEnNasb: And all the people were quarreling throughout the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king rescued us from the hands of our enemies and saved us from the hands of the Philistines, but now he has fled out of the land from Absalom.
verses.textEn: Throughout the tribes of Israel, all the people were arguing among themselves, saying, "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he is the one who rescued us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the country to escape from Absalom;

verses.textZh: 我们所膏立统治我们的押沙龙，已经在战场上死了。现在你们为甚么不出声请王回来呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 我们所膏立统治我们的押沙龙，已经在战场上死了。现在你们为甚么不出声请王回来呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 我们膏押沙龙治理我们，他已经阵亡。现在为什么不出一言请王回来呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: and Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"
verses.textEnEsv: But Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"
verses.textEnNkjv: But Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now therefore, why do you say nothing about bringing back the king?"
verses.textEnNlt: Now Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, is dead. Why not ask David to come back and be our king again?"
verses.textEnNasb: However, Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now then, why are you silent about bringing the king back?"
verses.textEn: and Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"

verses.textZh: 大卫王派人去见撒督祭司和亚比亚他，说："你们要对犹大的众长老说：‘你们为甚么在请王回宫的事上落在人后头呢？全以色列请王回宫的话已经传到王和王宫那里去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫王派人去见撒督祭司和亚比亚他，说："你们要对犹大的众长老说：‘你们为甚么在请王回宫的事上落在人后头呢？全以色列请王回宫的话已经传到王和王宫那里去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫王差人去见祭司撒督和亚比亚他，说：「你们当向犹大长老说：『以色列众人已经有话请王回宫，你们为什么落在他们后头呢？
verses.textEnNiv: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: "Ask the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace, since what is being said throughout Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
verses.textEnEsv: And King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Israel has come to the king?
verses.textEnNkjv: So King David sent to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house, since the words of all Israel have come to the king, to his very house?
verses.textEnNlt: Then King David sent Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, to say to the elders of Judah, "Why are you the last ones to welcome back the king into his palace? For I have heard that all Israel is ready.
verses.textEnNasb: Then King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house, since the word of all Israel has come to the king, even to his house?
verses.textEn: King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: "Ask the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his palace, since what is being said throughout Israel has reached the king at his quarters?

verses.textZh: 你们是我的兄弟，我的骨肉至亲，为甚么在请王回来的事上，倒落在人后头呢？’
verses.textZhCnvs: 你们是我的兄弟，我的骨肉至亲，为甚么在请王回来的事上，倒落在人后头呢？’
verses.textZhCuv: 你们是我的弟兄，是我的骨肉，为什么在人后头请王回来呢？』
verses.textEnNiv: You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring back the king?’
verses.textEnEsv: You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?’
verses.textEnNkjv: You are my brethren, you are my bone and my flesh. Why then are you the last to bring back the king?’
verses.textEnNlt: You are my relatives, my own tribe, my own flesh and blood! So why are you the last ones to welcome back the king?"
verses.textEnNasb: You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?’
verses.textEn: You are my relatives, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to bring back the king?’

verses.textZh: 你们又要对亚玛撒说：‘你不是我的骨肉至亲吗？我若不立你代替约押，在我面前作军队的元帅，愿神重重地惩罚我，并且加倍严厉地惩罚我。’"
verses.textZhCnvs: 你们又要对亚玛撒说：‘你不是我的骨肉至亲吗？我若不立你代替约押，在我面前作军队的元帅，愿神重重地惩罚我，并且加倍严厉地惩罚我。’"
verses.textZhCuv: 也要对亚玛撒说：『你不是我的骨肉吗？我若不立你替约押常作元帅，愿神重重地降罚与我！』」
verses.textEnNiv: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you are not the commander of my army for life in place of Joab.’ "
verses.textEnEsv: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me and more also, if you are not commander of my army from now on in place of Joab.’"
verses.textEnNkjv: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you are not commander of the army before me continually in place of Joab.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: And David told them to tell Amasa, "Since you are my own flesh and blood, like Joab, may God strike me and even kill me if I do not appoint you as commander of my army in his place."
verses.textEnNasb: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do so to me, and more so, if you will not be commander of the army for me continually, in place of Joab.’ "
verses.textEn: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my own flesh and blood? May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you are not the commander of my army for life in place of Joab.’ "

verses.textZh: 这样，大卫挽回了犹大众人的心，好象一人的心。于是他们差派人去见王，说："请你和你的众臣仆都回来！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 这样，大卫挽回了犹大众人的心，好象一人的心。于是他们差派人去见王，说："请你和你的众臣仆都回来！"
verses.textZhCuv: 如此就挽回犹大众人的心，如同一人的心。他们便打发人去见王，说：「请王和王的一切臣仆回来。」
verses.textEnNiv: He won over the hearts of the men of Judah so that they were all of one mind. They sent word to the king, "Return, you and all your men."
verses.textEnEsv: And he swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king, "Return, both you and all your servants."
verses.textEnNkjv: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah, just as theheartof one man, so that they sent thisword to the king: "Return, you and all your servants!"
verses.textEnNlt: Then Amasa convinced all the men of Judah, and they responded unanimously. They sent word to the king, "Return to us, and bring back all who are with you."
verses.textEnNasb: So he turned the hearts of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king, saying, "Return, you and all your servants."
verses.textEn: He won over the hearts of the men of Judah so that they were all of one mind. They sent word to the king, "Return, you and all your men."

verses.textZh: 王就回来，到了约旦河。犹大人也来到吉甲，要去迎接王，接王过约旦河。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王就回来，到了约旦河。犹大人也来到吉甲，要去迎接王，接王过约旦河。
verses.textZhCuv: 王就回来，到了约旦河。犹大人来到吉甲，要去迎接王，请他过约旦河。
verses.textEnNiv: Then the king returned and went as far as the Jordan. Now the men of Judah had come to Gilgal to go out and meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.
verses.textEnEsv: So the king came back to the Jordan, and Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring the king over the Jordan.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then the king returned and came to the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to escort the king across the Jordan.
verses.textEnNlt: So the king started back to Jerusalem. And when he arrived at the Jordan River, the people of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the river.
verses.textEnNasb: The king then returned and came as far as the Jordan. And the men of Judah came to Gilgal in order to go to meet the king, to escort the king across the Jordan.
verses.textEn: Then the king returned and went as far as the Jordan. Now the men of Judah had come to Gilgal to go out and meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.

verses.textZh: 巴户琳的便雅悯人，基拉的儿子示每，急忙与犹大人一同下去迎接大卫王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 巴户琳的便雅悯人，基拉的儿子示每，急忙与犹大人一同下去迎接大卫王。
verses.textZhCuv: 巴户琳的便雅悯人、基拉的儿子示每急忙与犹大人一同下去迎接大卫王。
verses.textEnNiv: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
verses.textEnEsv: And Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjaminite, from Bahurim, hurried to come down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
verses.textEnNkjv: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, who was from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
verses.textEnNlt: Shimei son of Gera, the man from Bahurim in Benjamin, hurried across with the men of Judah to welcome King David.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjaminite who was from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
verses.textEn: Shimei son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

verses.textZh: 与示每同来的有一千便雅悯人，还有扫罗家的仆人洗巴，和他的十五个儿子，以及二十个仆人。他们都冲过约旦河去迎接王。
verses.textZhCnvs: 与示每同来的有一千便雅悯人，还有扫罗家的仆人洗巴，和他的十五个儿子，以及二十个仆人。他们都冲过约旦河去迎接王。
verses.textZhCuv: 跟从示每的有一千便雅悯人，还有扫罗家的仆人洗巴和他十五个儿子，二十个仆人；他们都趟过约旦河迎接王。
verses.textEnNiv: With him were a thousand Benjamites, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul’s household, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan, where the king was.
verses.textEnEsv: And with him were a thousand men from Benjamin. And Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants, rushed down to the Jordan before the king,
verses.textEnNkjv: Therewere a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over the Jordan before the king.
verses.textEnNlt: A thousand other men from the tribe of Benjamin were with him, including Ziba, the chief servant of the house of Saul, and Ziba’s fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan to meet the king.
verses.textEnNasb: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they rushed to the Jordan before the king.
verses.textEn: With him were a thousand Benjamites, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul’s household, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to the Jordan, where the king was.

verses.textZh: 有人渡过渡口，把王的家眷接过去，并且照着王的心意去作。大卫过约旦河的时候，基拉的儿子示每俯伏在王面前，
verses.textZhCnvs: 有人渡过渡口，把王的家眷接过去，并且照着王的心意去作。大卫过约旦河的时候，基拉的儿子示每俯伏在王面前，
verses.textZhCuv: 有摆渡船过去，渡王的家眷，任王使用。 王要过约旦河的时候，基拉的儿子示每就俯伏在王面前，
verses.textEnNiv: They crossed at the ford to take the king’s household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king
verses.textEnEsv: and they crossed the ford to bring over the king’s household and to do his pleasure. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was about to cross the Jordan,
verses.textEnNkjv: Then a ferryboat went across to carry over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. Now Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king when he had crossed the Jordan.
verses.textEnNlt: They crossed the shallows of the Jordan to bring the king’s household across the river, helping him in every way they could. As the king was about to cross the river, Shimei fell down before him.
verses.textEnNasb: Then they crossed the shallow places repeatedly to bring over the king’s household, and to do what was good in his sight. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king as he was about to cross the Jordan.
verses.textEn: They crossed at the ford to take the king’s household over and to do whatever he wished. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell prostrate before the king

verses.textZh: 对王说："我主我王从耶路撒冷出来的那一天，你仆人所犯的错，现在求我主不要归罪于我，求你不要记念，求王也不要放在心上。
verses.textZhCnvs: 对王说："我主我王从耶路撒冷出来的那一天，你仆人所犯的错，现在求我主不要归罪于我，求你不要记念，求王也不要放在心上。
verses.textZhCuv: 对王说：「我主我王出耶路撒冷的时候，仆人行悖逆的事，现在求我主不要因此加罪与仆人，不要记念，也不要放在心上。
verses.textEnNiv: and said to him, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.
verses.textEnEsv: and said to the king, "Let not my lord hold me guilty or remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. Do not let the king take it to heart.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then he said to the king, "Do not let my lord impute iniquity to me, or remember what wrong your servant did on the day that my lord the king left Jerusalem, that the king should take it to heart.
verses.textEnNlt: "My lord the king, please forgive me," he pleaded. "Forget the terrible thing your servant did when you left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.
verses.textEnNasb: And he said to the king, "May my lord not consider me guilty, nor call to mind what your servant did wrong on the day when my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, so that the king would take it to heart.
verses.textEn: and said to him, "May my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.

verses.textZh: 因为你的仆人知道自己犯了罪，所以你看，在约瑟全家之中，今天我是第一个下来迎接我主我王的。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为你的仆人知道自己犯了罪，所以你看，在约瑟全家之中，今天我是第一个下来迎接我主我王的。"
verses.textZhCuv: 仆人明知自己有罪，所以约瑟全家之中，今日我首先下来迎接我主我王。」
verses.textEnNiv: For I your servant know that I have sinned, but today I have come here as the first from the tribes of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king."
verses.textEnEsv: For your servant knows that I have sinned. Therefore, behold, I have come this day, the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king."
verses.textEnNkjv: For I, your servant, know that I have sinned. Therefore here I am, the first to come today of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king."
verses.textEnNlt: I know how much I sinned. That is why I have come here today, the very first person in all Israel to greet my lord the king."
verses.textEnNasb: For your servant knows that I have sinned; so behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king."
verses.textEn: For I your servant know that I have sinned, but today I have come here as the first from the tribes of Joseph to come down and meet my lord the king."

verses.textZh: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛回答说："示每咒骂了耶和华的受膏者，岂不该因此把他处死吗？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛回答说："示每咒骂了耶和华的受膏者，岂不该因此把他处死吗？"
verses.textZhCuv: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛说：「示每既咒骂耶和华的受膏者，不应当治死他吗？」
verses.textEnNiv: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the Lord ’s anointed."
verses.textEnEsv: Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered, "Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord ’s anointed?"
verses.textEnNkjv: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord’s anointed?"
verses.textEnNlt: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shimei should die, for he cursed the Lord ’s anointed king!"
verses.textEnNasb: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah responded, "Should Shimei not be put to death for this, the fact that he cursed the Lord’s anointed?"
verses.textEn: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this? He cursed the Lord ’s anointed."

verses.textZh: 大卫说："洗鲁雅的儿子们啊，我与你们有甚么关系呢？今天你们竟与我作对！今天在以色列中，岂可有人被处死呢？难道我不知道今天我作以色列的王吗？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫说："洗鲁雅的儿子们啊，我与你们有甚么关系呢？今天你们竟与我作对！今天在以色列中，岂可有人被处死呢？难道我不知道今天我作以色列的王吗？"
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫说：「洗鲁雅的儿子，我与你们有何关涉，使你们今日与我反对呢？今日在以色列中岂可治死人呢？我岂不知今日我作以色列的王吗？」
verses.textEnNiv: David replied, "What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? What right do you have to interfere? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don’t I know that today I am king over Israel?"
verses.textEnEsv: But David said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be as an adversary to me? Shall anyone be put to death in Israel this day? For do I not know that I am this day king over Israel?"
verses.textEnNkjv: And David said, "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be adversaries to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Israel? For do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
verses.textEnNlt: "Who asked your opinion, you sons of Zeruiah!" David exclaimed. "Why have you become my adversary today? This is not a day for execution, for today I am once again the king of Israel!"
verses.textEnNasb: David then said, "What is there between you and me, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be an adversary to me today? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? For do I not know that I am king over Israel today?"
verses.textEn: David replied, "What does this have to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? What right do you have to interfere? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don’t I know that today I am king over Israel?"

verses.textZh: 于是王对示每说："你一定不会被处死！"王又向他起誓。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是王对示每说："你一定不会被处死！"王又向他起誓。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是王对示每说：「你必不死。」王就向他起誓。
verses.textEnNiv: So the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king promised him on oath.
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king gave him his oath.
verses.textEnNkjv: Therefore the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king swore to him.
verses.textEnNlt: Then, turning to Shimei, David vowed, "Your life will be spared."
verses.textEnNasb: So the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." The king also swore to him.
verses.textEn: So the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die." And the king promised him on oath.

verses.textZh: 扫罗的孙子米非波设也下去迎接王。他自从王出走那天，直到王平平安安回来的日子，都没有修脚，没有刮胡子，也没有洗衣服。
verses.textZhCnvs: 扫罗的孙子米非波设也下去迎接王。他自从王出走那天，直到王平平安安回来的日子，都没有修脚，没有刮胡子，也没有洗衣服。
verses.textZhCuv: 扫罗的孙子米非波设也下去迎接王。他自从王去的日子，直到王平平安安地回来，没有修脚，没有剃胡须，也没有洗衣服。
verses.textEnNiv: Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.
verses.textEnEsv: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had neither taken care of his feet nor trimmed his beard nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came back in safety.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. And he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his mustache, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he returned in peace.
verses.textEnNlt: Now Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, came down from Jerusalem to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes since the day the king left Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: Then Mephibosheth the grandson of Saul came down to meet the king; but he had neither tended to his feet, nor trimmed his mustache, nor washed his clothes since the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.
verses.textEn: Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, also went down to meet the king. He had not taken care of his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.

verses.textZh: 他从耶路撒冷来迎接王的时候，王问他："米非波设啊，你为甚么没有与我一同离开呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 他从耶路撒冷来迎接王的时候，王问他："米非波设啊，你为甚么没有与我一同离开呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 他来到耶路撒冷迎接王的时候，王问他说：「米非波设，你为什么没有与我同去呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.textEnEsv: And when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.textEnNkjv: So it was, when he had come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.textEnNlt: "Why didn’t you come with me, Mephibosheth?" the king asked him.
verses.textEnNasb: And it was when he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.textEn: When he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, the king asked him, "Why didn’t you go with me, Mephibosheth?"

verses.textZh: 他回答："我主我王，你仆人是瘸腿的；那天，我心里想我要预备驴子，可以骑上，与王一同离开，但是我的仆人却欺骗了我，
verses.textZhCnvs: 他回答："我主我王，你仆人是瘸腿的；那天，我心里想我要预备驴子，可以骑上，与王一同离开，但是我的仆人却欺骗了我，
verses.textZhCuv: 他回答说：「我主我王，仆人是瘸腿的。那日我想要备驴骑上，与王同去，无奈我的仆人欺哄了我，
verses.textEnNiv: He said, "My lord the king, since I your servant am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled and will ride on it, so I can go with the king.’ But Ziba my servant betrayed me.
verses.textEnEsv: He answered, "My lord, O king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said to him, ‘I will saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ For your servant is lame.
verses.textEnNkjv: And he answered, "My lord, O king, my servant deceived me. For your servant said, ‘I will saddle a donkey for myself, that I may ride on it and go to the king,’ because your servant is lame.
verses.textEnNlt: Mephibosheth replied, "My lord the king, my servant Ziba deceived me. I told him, ‘Saddle my donkey so I can go with the king.’ For as you know I am crippled.
verses.textEnNasb: So he said, "My lord the king, my servant betrayed me; for your servant said, ‘I will saddle the donkey for myself so that I may ride on it and go with the king,’ since your servant cannot walk.
verses.textEn: He said, "My lord the king, since I your servant am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled and will ride on it, so I can go with the king.’ But Ziba my servant betrayed me.

verses.textZh: 又在我主我王面前毁谤你仆人。但我主我王像神的使者一样，现在，你看怎样好，就怎样行吧！
verses.textZhCnvs: 又在我主我王面前毁谤你仆人。但我主我王像神的使者一样，现在，你看怎样好，就怎样行吧！
verses.textZhCuv: 又在我主我王面前谗毁我。然而我主我王如同神的使者一般，你看怎样好，就怎样行吧！
verses.textEnNiv: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king is like an angel of God; so do whatever you wish.
verses.textEnEsv: He has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like the angel of God; do therefore what seems good to you.
verses.textEnNkjv: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king, but my lord the king is like the angel of God. Therefore do whatis good in your eyes.
verses.textEnNlt: Ziba has slandered me by saying that I refused to come. But I know that my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do what you think is best.
verses.textEnNasb: Furthermore, he has slandered your servant to my lord the king; but my lord the king is like the angel of God, therefore do what is good in your sight.
verses.textEn: And he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. My lord the king is like an angel of God; so do whatever you wish.

verses.textZh: 因为我祖父全家的人，在我主我王面前都算不得甚么，都不过是该死的人；你却使仆人在你席上与你一同吃饭。我还有甚么权利再向王哀求甚么呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 因为我祖父全家的人，在我主我王面前都算不得甚么，都不过是该死的人；你却使仆人在你席上与你一同吃饭。我还有甚么权利再向王哀求甚么呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 因为我祖全家的人，在我主我王面前都算为死人，王却使仆人在王的席上同人吃饭，我现在向王还能辨理诉冤吗？」
verses.textEnNiv: All my grandfather’s descendants deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you gave your servant a place among those who eat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?"
verses.textEnEsv: For all my father’s house were but men doomed to death before my lord the king, but you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right have I, then, to cry to the king?"
verses.textEnNkjv: For all my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king. Yet you set your servant among those who eat at your own table. Therefore what right have I still to cry out anymore to the king?"
verses.textEnNlt: All my relatives and I could expect only death from you, my lord, but instead you have honored me by allowing me to eat at your own table! What more can I ask?"
verses.textEnNasb: For all my father’s household was only people worthy of death to my lord the king; yet you placed your servant among those who ate at your own table. So what right do I still have, that I should complain anymore to the king?"
verses.textEn: All my grandfather’s descendants deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, but you gave your servant a place among those who eat at your table. So what right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?"

verses.textZh: 王就对他说："你为甚么再提你的事呢？我已经决定，你与洗巴要均分那地。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王就对他说："你为甚么再提你的事呢？我已经决定，你与洗巴要均分那地。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王对他说：「你何必再提你的事呢？我说，你与洗巴均分地土。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king said to him, "Why say more? I order you and Ziba to divide the land."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said to him, "Why speak any more of your affairs? I have decided: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
verses.textEnNkjv: So the king said to him, "Why do you speak anymore of your matters? I have said, ‘You and Ziba divide the land.’ "
verses.textEnNlt: "You’ve said enough," David replied. "I’ve decided that you and Ziba will divide your land equally between you."
verses.textEnNasb: So the king said to him, "Why do you still speak of your affairs? I have decided, ‘You and Ziba shall divide the land.’ "
verses.textEn: The king said to him, "Why say more? I order you and Ziba to divide the land."

verses.textZh: 米非波设对王说："我主我王既然已平平安安回宫，所有的一切就都任凭洗巴拿去好了。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 米非波设对王说："我主我王既然已平平安安回宫，所有的一切就都任凭洗巴拿去好了。"
verses.textZhCuv: 米非波设对王说：「我主我王既平平安安地回宫，就任凭洗巴都取了也可以。」
verses.textEnNiv: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has returned home safely."
verses.textEnEsv: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Oh, let him take it all, since my lord the king has come safely home."
verses.textEnNkjv: Then Mephibosheth said to the king, "Rather, let him take it all, inasmuch as my lord the king has come back in peace to his own house."
verses.textEnNlt: "Give him all of it," Mephibosheth said. "I am content just to have you safely back again, my lord the king!"
verses.textEnNasb: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him even take it all, since my lord the king has come safely to his own house."
verses.textEn: Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take everything, now that my lord the king has returned home safely."

verses.textZh: 基列人巴西莱也从罗基琳下来，与王一同过约旦河，要在约旦河边给王送行。
verses.textZhCnvs: 基列人巴西莱也从罗基琳下来，与王一同过约旦河，要在约旦河边给王送行。
verses.textZhCuv: 基列人巴西莱从罗基琳下来，要送王过约旦河，就与王一同过了约旦河。
verses.textEnNiv: Barzillai the Gileadite also came down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and to send him on his way from there.
verses.textEnEsv: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim, and he went on with the king to the Jordan, to escort him over the Jordan.
verses.textEnNkjv: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and went across the Jordan with the king, to escort him across the Jordan.
verses.textEnNlt: Barzillai of Gilead had come down from Rogelim to escort the king across the Jordan.
verses.textEnNasb: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim; and he went on to the Jordan with the king to escort him over the Jordan.
verses.textEn: Barzillai the Gileadite also came down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and to send him on his way from there.

verses.textZh: 巴西莱年纪非常老迈，已经八十岁。王住在玛哈念的时候，是他供养王的，因为他是一个很富有的人。
verses.textZhCnvs: 巴西莱年纪非常老迈，已经八十岁。王住在玛哈念的时候，是他供养王的，因为他是一个很富有的人。
verses.textZhCuv: 巴西莱年纪老迈，已经八十岁了。王住在玛哈念的时候，他就拿食物来供给王；他原是大富户。
verses.textEnNiv: Now Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had provided for the king during his stay in Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
verses.textEnEsv: Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. He had provided the king with food while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. And he had provided the king with supplies while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very rich man.
verses.textEnNlt: He was very old—eighty years of age—and very wealthy. He was the one who had provided food for the king during his stay in Mahanaim.
verses.textEnNasb: Barzillai was very old: eighty years old; and he had provided the king food while he stayed in Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.
verses.textEn: Now Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had provided for the king during his stay in Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.

verses.textZh: 王对巴西莱说："你与我一同过河去，在耶路撒冷与我同住，我要供养你。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王对巴西莱说："你与我一同过河去，在耶路撒冷与我同住，我要供养你。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王对巴西莱说：「你与我同去，我要在耶路撒冷那里养你的老。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and stay with me in Jerusalem, and I will provide for you."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king said to Barzillai, "Come over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king said to Barzillai, "Come across with me, and I will provide for you while you are with me in Jerusalem."
verses.textEnNlt: "Come across with me and live in Jerusalem," the king said to Barzillai. "I will take care of you there."
verses.textEnNasb: So the king said to Barzillai, "You cross over with me, and I will provide you food in Jerusalem with me."
verses.textEn: The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and stay with me in Jerusalem, and I will provide for you."

verses.textZh: 巴西莱对王说："我活着的年日还能有多少，可使我与王一同上耶路撒冷呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 巴西莱对王说："我活着的年日还能有多少，可使我与王一同上耶路撒冷呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 巴西莱对王说：「我在世的年日还能有多少，使我与王同上耶路撒冷呢？
verses.textEnNiv: But Barzillai answered the king, "How many more years will I live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
verses.textEnEsv: But Barzillai said to the king, "How many years have I still to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.textEnNkjv: But Barzillai said to the king, "How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.textEnNlt: "No," he replied, "I am far too old to go with the king to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: But Barzillai said to the king, "How long do I still have to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.textEn: But Barzillai answered the king, "How many more years will I live, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?

verses.textZh: 我现在已经八十岁了，还能分别美丑吗？你仆人还能尝出吃喝的味道吗？我还能细听男女歌手的声音吗？你仆人为甚么要负累我主我王呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 我现在已经八十岁了，还能分别美丑吗？你仆人还能尝出吃喝的味道吗？我还能细听男女歌手的声音吗？你仆人为甚么要负累我主我王呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 仆人现在八十岁了，还能尝出饮食的滋味、辨别美恶吗？还能听男女歌唱的声音吗？仆人何必累赘我主我王呢？
verses.textEnNiv: I am now eighty years old. Can I tell the difference between what is enjoyable and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of male and female singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
verses.textEnEsv: I am this day eighty years old. Can I discern what is pleasant and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or what he drinks? Can I still listen to the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
verses.textEnNkjv: I am today eighty years old. Can I discern between the good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Can I hear any longer the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?
verses.textEnNlt: I am eighty years old today, and I can no longer enjoy anything. Food and wine are no longer tasty, and I cannot hear the singers as they sing. I would only be a burden to my lord the king.
verses.textEnNasb: I am now eighty years old. Can I distinguish between good and bad? Or can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Or can I still hear the voice of men and women singing? Why then should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
verses.textEn: I am now eighty years old. Can I tell the difference between what is enjoyable and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats and drinks? Can I still hear the voices of male and female singers? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?

verses.textZh: 你仆人只不过与王一同过约旦河，王为甚么要这样赏赐我呢？
verses.textZhCnvs: 你仆人只不过与王一同过约旦河，王为甚么要这样赏赐我呢？
verses.textZhCuv: 仆人只要送王过约旦河，王何必赐我这样的恩典呢？
verses.textEnNiv: Your servant will cross over the Jordan with the king for a short distance, but why should the king reward me in this way?
verses.textEnEsv: Your servant will go a little way over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?
verses.textEnNkjv: Your servant will go a little way across the Jordan with the king. And why should the king repay me with such a reward?
verses.textEnNlt: Just to go across the Jordan River with the king is all the honor I need!
verses.textEnNasb: Your servant would merely cross over the Jordan with the king. So why should the king compensate me with this reward?
verses.textEn: Your servant will cross over the Jordan with the king for a short distance, but why should the king reward me in this way?

verses.textZh: 请让你仆人回去，好死在我自己的城里，埋葬在我父母的坟墓旁。看哪，你仆人金罕在这里，请让他与我主我王一同过河；你看怎么好，就怎么待他吧！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 请让你仆人回去，好死在我自己的城里，埋葬在我父母的坟墓旁。看哪，你仆人金罕在这里，请让他与我主我王一同过河；你看怎么好，就怎么待他吧！"
verses.textZhCuv: 求你准我回去，好死在我本城，葬在我父母的墓旁。这里有王的仆人金罕，让他同我主我王过去，可以随意待他。」
verses.textEnNiv: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever you wish."
verses.textEnEsv: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him go over with my lord the king, and do for him whatever seems good to you."
verses.textEnNkjv: Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my own city, near the grave of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what seems good to you."
verses.textEnNlt: Then let me return again to die in my own town, where my father and mother are buried. But here is your servant, my son Kimham. Let him go with my lord the king and receive whatever you want to give him."
verses.textEnNasb: Please let your servant return, so that I may die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. However, here is your servant Chimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight."
verses.textEn: Let your servant return, that I may die in my own town near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever you wish."

verses.textZh: 王说："金罕可以与我一同过河。你看怎么好，我就怎么待他。你向我所要求的，我都必为你成全。"
verses.textZhCnvs: 王说："金罕可以与我一同过河。你看怎么好，我就怎么待他。你向我所要求的，我都必为你成全。"
verses.textZhCuv: 王说：「金罕可以与我同去，我必照你的心愿待他。你向我求什么，我都必为你成就。」
verses.textEnNiv: The king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And anything you desire from me I will do for you."
verses.textEnEsv: And the king answered, "Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do for him whatever seems good to you, and all that you desire of me I will do for you."
verses.textEnNkjv: And the king answered, "Chimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good to you. Now whatever you request of me, I will do for you."
verses.textEnNlt: "Good," the king agreed. "Kimham will go with me, and I will help him in any way you would like. And I will do for you anything you want."
verses.textEnNasb: And the king answered, "Chimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your sight; and whatever you require of me, I will do for you."
verses.textEn: The king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever you wish. And anything you desire from me I will do for you."

verses.textZh: 于是众人都渡过约旦河，王也渡过了。王与巴西莱亲吻，为他祝福，巴西莱就回自己的地方去了。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是众人都渡过约旦河，王也渡过了。王与巴西莱亲吻，为他祝福，巴西莱就回自己的地方去了。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是众民过约旦河，王也过去。王与巴西莱亲嘴，为他祝福，巴西莱就回本地去了。
verses.textEnNiv: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and bid him farewell, and Barzillai returned to his home.
verses.textEnEsv: Then all the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over. And the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own home.
verses.textEnNkjv: Then all the people went over the Jordan. And when the king had crossed over, the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.
verses.textEnNlt: So all the people crossed the Jordan with the king. After David had blessed Barzillai and kissed him, Barzillai returned to his own home.
verses.textEnNasb: All the people crossed over the Jordan and the king crossed too. The king then kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.
verses.textEn: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and bid him farewell, and Barzillai returned to his home.

verses.textZh: 王过了河，到了吉甲，金罕也与王一同渡河。所有的犹大人和半数以色列人，也都与王一同渡河。
verses.textZhCnvs: 王过了河，到了吉甲，金罕也与王一同渡河。所有的犹大人和半数以色列人，也都与王一同渡河。
verses.textZhCuv: 王过去，到了吉甲，金罕也跟他过去。犹大众民和以色列民的一半也都送王过去。
verses.textEnNiv: When the king crossed over to Gilgal, Kimham crossed with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel had taken the king over.
verses.textEnEsv: The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. All the people of Judah, and also half the people of Israel, brought the king on his way.
verses.textEnNkjv: Now the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. And all the people of Judah escorted the king, and also half the people of Israel.
verses.textEnNlt: The king then crossed over to Gilgal, taking Kimham with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king on his way.
verses.textEnNasb: Now the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him; and all the people of Judah and also half the people of Israel accompanied the king.
verses.textEn: When the king crossed over to Gilgal, Kimham crossed with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel had taken the king over.

verses.textZh: 以色列众人都来见王，问王说："我们的兄弟犹大人为甚么把你偷去了，把王和王的家眷接过约旦河呢？属大卫的人不都一样是他的人民吗？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 以色列众人都来见王，问王说："我们的兄弟犹大人为甚么把你偷去了，把王和王的家眷接过约旦河呢？属大卫的人不都一样是他的人民吗？"
verses.textZhCuv: 以色列众人来见王，对他说：「我们弟兄犹大人为什么暗暗送王和王的家眷，并跟随王的人过约旦河？」
verses.textEnNiv: Soon all the men of Israel were coming to the king and saying to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, together with all his men?"
verses.textEnEsv: Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?"
verses.textEnNkjv: Just then all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, "Why have our brethren, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king, his household, and all David’s men with him across the Jordan?"
verses.textEnNlt: But all the men of Israel complained to the king, "The men of Judah stole the king and didn’t give us the honor of helping take you, your household, and all your men across the Jordan."
verses.textEnNasb: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, abducted you and brought the king and his household and all David’s men with him, over the Jordan?"
verses.textEn: Soon all the men of Israel were coming to the king and saying to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal the king away and bring him and his household across the Jordan, together with all his men?"

verses.textZh: 犹大众人回答以色列人说："因为王与我们的关系亲密。你们为甚么因这事而生气呢？我们从王那里得到甚么吃的呢？或是他给了我们甚么礼物呢？"
verses.textZhCnvs: 犹大众人回答以色列人说："因为王与我们的关系亲密。你们为甚么因这事而生气呢？我们从王那里得到甚么吃的呢？或是他给了我们甚么礼物呢？"
verses.textZhCuv: 犹大众人回答以色列人说：「因为王与我们是亲属，你们为何因这事发怒呢？我们吃了王的什么呢？王赏赐了我们什么呢？」
verses.textEnNiv: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "We did this because the king is closely related to us. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten any of the king’s provisions? Have we taken anything for ourselves?"
verses.textEnEsv: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king’s expense? Or has he given us any gift?"
verses.textEnNkjv: So all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is a close relative of ours. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense? Or has he given us any gift?"
verses.textEnNlt: The men of Judah replied, "The king is one of our own kinsmen. Why should this make you angry? We haven’t eaten any of the king’s food or received any special favors!"
verses.textEnNasb: Then all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king’s expense, or has anything been taken for us?"
verses.textEn: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "We did this because the king is closely related to us. Why are you angry about it? Have we eaten any of the king’s provisions? Have we taken anything for ourselves?"

verses.textZh: 以色列人回答犹大人说："在王的事上，我们有十分的投入。在大卫身上，我们也与大卫比你们更有情分。你们为甚么轻视我们呢？先说要请我们的王回来的，不是我们吗？"但是犹大人的话比以色列人的话更强硬。
verses.textZhCnvs: 以色列人回答犹大人说："在王的事上，我们有十分的投入。在大卫身上，我们也与大卫比你们更有情分。你们为甚么轻视我们呢？先说要请我们的王回来的，不是我们吗？"但是犹大人的话比以色列人的话更强硬。
verses.textZhCuv: 以色列人回答犹大人说：「按支派，我们与王有十分的情分；在大卫身上，我们也比你们更有情分。你们为何藐视我们，请王回来不先与我们商量呢？」 但犹大人的话比以色列人的话更硬。
verses.textEnNiv: Then the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king; so we have a greater claim on David than you have. Why then do you treat us with contempt? Weren’t we the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah pressed their claims even more forcefully than the men of Israel.
verses.textEnEsv: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, and in David also we have more than you. Why then did you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.textEnNkjv: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, "We have ten shares in the king; therefore we also have more right to David than you. Why then do you despise us—were we not the first to advise bringing back our king?" Yet the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.textEnNlt: "But there are ten tribes in Israel," the others replied. "So we have ten times as much right to the king as you do. What right do you have to treat us with such contempt? Weren’t we the first to speak of bringing him back to be our king again?" The argument continued back and forth, and the men of Judah spoke even more harshly than the men of Israel.
verses.textEnNasb: But the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, " We have ten parts in the king, therefore we also have more claim on David than you. Why then did you treat us with contempt? Was it not our advice first to bring back our king?" Yet the words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel.
verses.textEn: Then the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king; so we have a greater claim on David than you have. Why then do you treat us with contempt? Weren’t we the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah pressed their claims even more forcefully than the men of Israel.

verses.textZh: 在那里恰巧有一个流氓名叫示巴，是便雅悯人比基利的儿子。他吹号角，说： "我们在大卫的身上无分， 在耶西的儿子身上无干， 以色列人哪！各回自己的帐棚去吧！"
verses.textZhCnvs: 在那里恰巧有一个流氓名叫示巴，是便雅悯人比基利的儿子。他吹号角，说： "我们在大卫的身上无分， 在耶西的儿子身上无干， 以色列人哪！各回自己的帐棚去吧！"
verses.textZhCuv: 在那里恰巧有一个匪徒，名叫示巴，是便雅悯人比基利的儿子。他吹角，说：「我们与大卫无分，与耶西的儿子无涉。以色列人哪，你们各回各家去吧！」
verses.textEnNiv: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bikri, a Benjamite, happened to be there. He sounded the trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David, no part in Jesse’s son! Every man to his tent, Israel!"
verses.textEnEsv: Now there happened to be there a worthless man, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. And he blew the trumpet and said, "We have no portion in David, and we have no inheritance in the son of Jesse; every man to his tents, O Israel!"
verses.textEnNkjv: And there happened to be there a rebel, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite. And he blew a trumpet, and said: "We have no share in David, Nor do we have inheritance in the son of Jesse; Every man to his tents, O Israel!"
verses.textEnNlt: There happened to be a troublemaker there named Sheba son of Bicri, a man from the tribe of Benjamin. Sheba blew a ram’s horn and began to chant: "Down with the dynasty of David! We have no interest in the son of Jesse. Come on, you men of Israel, back to your homes!"
verses.textEnNasb: Now a worthless man happened to be there whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite; and he blew the trumpet and said, "We have no share in David, Nor do we have an inheritance in the son of Jesse; Every man to his tents, Israel!"
verses.textEn: Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bikri, a Benjamite, happened to be there. He sounded the trumpet and shouted, "We have no share in David, no part in Jesse’s son! Every man to his tent, Israel!"

verses.textZh: 于是以色列众人都上山去，不跟随大卫，却跟随了比基利的儿子示巴；犹大人却紧紧跟随他们的王，从约旦河直到耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCnvs: 于是以色列众人都上山去，不跟随大卫，却跟随了比基利的儿子示巴；犹大人却紧紧跟随他们的王，从约旦河直到耶路撒冷。
verses.textZhCuv: 于是以色列人都离开大卫，跟随比基利的儿子示巴。但犹大人从约旦河直到耶路撒冷，都紧紧跟随他们的王。
verses.textEnNiv: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bikri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnEsv: So all the men of Israel withdrew from David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah followed their king steadfastly from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNkjv: So every man of Israel deserted David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah, from the Jordan as far as Jerusalem, remained loyal to their king.
verses.textEnNlt: So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed with their king and escorted him from the Jordan River to Jerusalem.
verses.textEnNasb: So all the men of Israel withdrew from following David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah remained loyal to their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.textEn: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bikri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

verses.textZh: 大卫王回到耶路撒冷自己的宫里，就把以前留下来看守王宫的那十个妃嫔捉起来，关在禁宫里。王供养她们，却不再亲近她们。她们被禁闭，过着寡妇一般的生活，直到死的日子。
verses.textZhCnvs: 大卫王回到耶路撒冷自己的宫里，就把以前留下来看守王宫的那十个妃嫔捉起来，关在禁宫里。王供养她们，却不再亲近她们。她们被禁闭，过着寡妇一般的生活，直到死的日子。
verses.textZhCuv: 大卫王来到耶路撒冷，进了宫殿，就把从前留下看守宫殿的十个妃嫔禁闭在冷宫，养活她们，不与她们亲近。她们如同寡妇被禁，直到死的日子。
verses.textEnNiv: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace and put them in a house under guard. He provided for them but had no sexual relations with them. They were kept in confinement till the day of their death, living as widows.
verses.textEnEsv: And David came to his house at Jerusalem. And the king took the ten concubines whom he had left to care for the house and put them in a house under guard and provided for them, but did not go in to them. So they were shut up until the day of their death, living as if in widowhood.
